- ### Explore on your schedule



Start and stop VoiceMap tours whenever you like, instead of being herded along in a group. Grab a drink, take in the view, then tap Resume to pick up exactly where you left off.


- ### Automatic GPS playback



Focus on your surroundings, not the screen, with turn-by-turn direction and audio that plays automatically at the right time and place. Just tap on Start, and let VoiceMap guide you.


- ### Use the app offline



Avoid expensive roaming fees or fiddly connection issues by downloading VoiceMap tours in advance. They work offline and include offline maps.


- ### Listen as often as you like



Enjoy tours as many times as you like, both in your destination and with your feet up, at home. Virtual playback turns every tour into an audio book.

> Great commentary in a real, human voice, good selection of places to see. - ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

> Absolutely the best way to navigate through key landmarks / regions of a city with your own personal your guide patiently sharing exclusive tips & stories. Pause, spend more time in one location then resume when ready. Get all the best of sightseeing without feeling like "a tourist"

- ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

> We have done a few of these tours in the UK, Italy and France. They are an excellent way of introducing yourself to a town and learning a bit about its history and culture. Some have some tasty food stops along the way. We’d highly recommended this app

- ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

> I do VoiceMap wherever I travel. I love it. One time I made the mistake of doing a group tour and it was three times as much and not very engjoyable. VoiceMap is great because I can go at my own pace. I always am able to understand the speaker as they're in my ear. And if I want to stop and explore and see something and come back, I can. I can also do it at any time of day. Sometimes I do it in the middle of the night. Sometimes I do VoiceMap in the morning. It's so nice.

- ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

> I have done dozens of VoiceMap tours, and I think I can say this is the best. It gives an incredible feeling of place and culture, combining respectful humour with insight into history and the evolution of Hutongs in recent years.

- ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

> Felicity’s voice is just lovely and her explanations are great, full of anecdotal & curious detail as well as the necessary background needed to understand how this park came to be; why it was - and remains - so important for madrileños, and how it fits in the puzzle of Madrid’s geography & history. Really enjoyed wandering around with my headphones on while listening to the guided tour!

- ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

> Really enjoyed this tour! I GPS worked perfectly. The content was riveting. I think I only pulled out my phone once or twice!

- ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

> A variety of things to see in the city, combined with the stories behind them, really drew me into Amsterdam’s roaring past. The more recent stories about the city were also amusing and interesting, and all told with warmth and heart.

- ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

- ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/reputation/quote-4544c3f0a259674f5c3557531a98464490d95a7f8d1a7348091087512c3f0083.svg)

### A marketplace with built-in discovery and distribution

VoiceMap is the leading app for self-guided audio tours. It’s optimised for discovery, tops App Store and Google Play rankings, and it offers distribution through a wide network of partners.

![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/partner/block-2-402223649331f5fdcb3219795a33e1fbe27f1da14f2804451bdbf4962fad5153.png)

### Partners from map to mic to market

We know what works from experience and we’ll help you through every step of publishing and promoting the perfect tour.

![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/partner/block-3-04ecb24e787a1de7535835bf985184c1354bd89ca55daccf6b347eacf399d884.png)

### Make your tours public or private, paid or free

Mix and match distribution options. Sell your tour, give it away to guests, or keep it private and build it into other products. It’s up to you.

![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/home/partner/block-4-65af1c207074c361956979f6eaf2872c9bc06cc5986fbcced800db505a198f06.png)

### Live reporting, regular payments

Our dashboard for publishers makes it easy to track key metrics like ratings, downloads and sales. You can manage vouchers there too, as well as monthly payments.

# Self Guided Walking Tours

[![](https://www.gpsmycity.com/d/getapp_itunes_icon.png)](https://www.gpsmycity.com/dlnk/?act=store&go=itunes)[![](https://www.gpsmycity.com/d/getapp_gplay_icon.png)](https://www.gpsmycity.com/dlnk/?act=store&go=gplay)[![](https://www.gpsmycity.com/d/getapp_qrcode_icon.png)](https://me-qr.com/nd6BMfe2)

GPSmyCity app is a pocket tour guide that brings GPS-powered self-guided walking tours and travel tips for **[1,800+ cities](https://www.gpsmycity.com/gps-tour-guides/index.html)** worldwide. No internet. No tour groups. Just explore the cities your way. This handy app presents you over **[7,000 self-guided walks](https://www.gpsmycity.com/gps-tour-guides/index.html)**.

## Frequently asked questions

#### How does it work without cell signal?

Our app uses GPS co-ordinates to determine your location and play commentary, not cellular or Wi-Fi signal.

Just pre-download both the app and tour content (audio, maps and images) to your phone, well before you leave signal, so you’ll have everything ready to tour offline.

And as there’s no time limit to use the tours, you can preview the tour routes, major highlights, itineraries and other travel tips as part of your trip planning.

#### How do I buy tours?

**BUY DIRECT & SAVE:**

1. From our webstore, sign in to unlock tours to your existing Apple or Google Play store profile.
2. Buy tours or bundles directly from GuideAlong and enter your payment method on our secure Stripe site.
3. Download the GuideAlong app from the link within your receipt. Sign in using the same Apple or Google Play store ID.
4. Open the Guidealong app and view your tour collection in the My Tours tab. Browse route maps, highlights, trip planners and other travel tips.

**BUY IN-APP FROM APPLE OR GOOGLE PLAY STORE ACCOUNT:**

1. Download the free GuideAlong app from the Apple or Google Play store and sign-in using your Apple or Google Play store ID.
2. Tap the Explore menu to view (unpurchased) tours and bundles.
3. Tap to BUY tours or bundles. Apple or Google Play manage transactions and payment methods.

#### Can it help me plan my trip?

Condensed Trip Planners are available in app with full versions available on our website for download.

Contents include

How to Get Here

Getting Around

Entrance Fees

Where to Stay

When to Visit

How Much Time Do You Need

How to Avoid the Crowds

Things to See and Do

Best Hikes

Family Fun Adventure

Awesome Experiences

Best Sunset and Sunrise Spots

Food You Have to Try

Packing List

Top Travel Tips

#### What languages do you offer?

Only English at this time, but keep watching …

#### Can I gift a tour?

Aren’t you nice! Yes, you sure can, just head over to our [store](https://store.guidealong.com/cart/) and toggle on “send tours as a gift” option.

#### Is there a time or date limit?

Tours are a one-time purchase with no date/time limit or expiry.  That’s right, no need to worry about using it within a certain timeframe.

And guess what? We’re always improving and updating our tours, so you can keep enjoying them. That’s just one of the ways we show our appreciation for your support.

#### How much does it cost?

Each tour is priced individually and listed on the tour page.

Tours and bundles are one time purchase, with no time/date limits or expiry and include free updates.

There’s no monthly subscriptions.

Make sure to check out the bundles to save even more!

#### Do I have to follow a set itinerary?

Our tours are designed to be flexible, so you can divide the commentary and customize into your own half, full or multi sightseeing day trips.

#### What devices will it work on?

All mobile devices that include a GPS chip and meet the minimum operating system requirements.

Apple iPad wifi models and Kindle Fire do not include a GPS chip and are prevented from downloading as they will not determine location in remote areas.

#### Will it work alongside music and navigational apps?

Our app works in background mode, allowing you to listen to your own road trip playlists.

Commentary will automatically pause or lower the volume of your music at triggered audio points.

Navigation is included as part of the narration, providing advanced notice on critical intersections, recommended side trips, as well as the best scenic viewpoints, along the tour routes.

If you do use another navigational app at the same time, (say to direct you to a specific restaurant or hotel) be aware they may direct you off our touring route.

[VIEW MORE](https://guidealong.com/faq/)

App Features

## Everything You Need to Explore History

Our app puts the power of historical discovery in your pocket with intuitive features designed for curious explorers.

### Comprehensive & Compelling Tours

Follow expertly crafted routes and dive into local history and culture at every stop.

### Then & Now Photography

Stand in the footsteps of historic photographers & use the camera to blend past and present.

### Audio Narration

Listen to engaging audio stories as you explore, bringing local history to life.

### Scavenger Hunts

Solve brain-teasing puzzles, uncover history's mysteries, and unlock achievements.

### Indigenous Video Tours

Watch Indigenous Knowledge-keepers share sacred knowledge in video tours.

### Virtual Tours

Explore a location from the comfort of home with 360° Virtual Tours.

### Audio Driving Tours

Listen to a region's history as you drive across it with GPS-activated hands-free audio tours.

### Biking Itineraries

Enhance your cycling adventure with curated itineraries that showcase history, culture, and attractions.

### Offline Mode

Leave worries about data or network service behind as you explore in offline mode.

Simple & Intuitive

## Partner with us to tell your Community's Story

1

### High Quality Content Creation

Let our team of talented researchers, writers, photographers, and videographers bring your community's story to life.

2

### Low-Cost Hosting

Make On This Spot your digital home by hosting your community's stories, tours, and attractions on our app and web platforms.

3

### State-of-the-Art CMS

Use our Content Management System to seamlessly add, update, edit, and customize your tours and points of interest.

4

### Flexible Partnerships

We want to ensure everyone who wants to can get on the app and have a huge range of flexible partnership options to fit every budget.

5

### Access our Growing Audience

Get your community put in front of our tens of thousands of users who rely on On This Spot to explore all that Canada has to offer.

6

### White Label & Custom Apps

Want your own app? We can design one for you!

Testimonials

## What Partners are Saying...

> "During the launch the app received a lot of public and media attention, and ultimately was a great success!... This is a unique digital tool for the City of Winnipeg and heritage tourism, while allowing for exposure all over the world. During the many months of collaboration there was good communication, and once funding was secured it was completed on time, and on budget."

Cindy Tugwell, Executive Director

Heritage Winnipeg

> "The On This Spot app definitely provides value and opportunity to cities, such as Nanaimo who are wanting to share their cultural or industrial history with both the visitors to their city as well as with the local citizenry... Through this partnership, we were able to help develop a product that provides a truly exceptional experience...""

Dan Brady, Executive Director

Tourism Nanaimo

> "The end product has manifested positive outcomes well beyond our initial agreement and expectations... The walking tour app has been embraced by our senior population who view it as an expression of respect... local educators to utilize the app as part of their curriculum.. What began as a simple initiative to showcase the history of our little town has become an exciting venture."

Rhonda Stockwell, Chair

Western District Historical Society

For Organizations

## Partner With Us Today

Let's work together to create exciting digital experiences in your community and share them with the world!

Contact Our Team
[Book a Demo Now](https://onthisspot.zohobookings.com/#/customer/andrew)

For Explorers

Download our free app and discover the hidden stories in your city. Available on iOS and Android with tours across 100+ cities in North America and Europe.

## How It Works

### Get the Full Story

Just Ahead audio guides are written by expert authors and narrated by professionals. You simply drive, while Just Ahead informs and entertains you.

![gps](https://www.justahead.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/gps.png)

#### GPS-guided tour

As you drive in your car or travel by train or bus, Just Ahead takes you on a guided tour. It uses GPS to know exactly where you are and what to say. Imagine you’re cresting a hill and in front of you is a beautiful sight. You’re wondering what it is. That’s when Just Ahead shares with you an exciting story about what you’re looking at.

#### Works offline

Many of the most beautiful places in the world don’t have mobile phone service. Just Ahead is designed to work wherever you are, even without WiFi or a cell signal. Just be sure to download your guide before you go on your trip.

![works-offline](https://www.justahead.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/works-offline.png)

![maps](https://www.justahead.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/maps.png)

#### Built-in maps

Don’t you hate it when you try to use the maps on your smartphone and they don’t work because there’s no mobile phone service? No worries. Each Just Ahead guide comes bundled with an offline version of the maps you need, even without Internet access.

#### Great stories

Just Ahead guides are written by expert authors and filled with fascinating stories of history, geology, and wildlife. You can’t read and drive. It’s crazy, illegal, and will probably make you sick. Let us guide and inform you as you drive.

![stories](https://www.justahead.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/stories.png)

![turn-by-turn](https://www.justahead.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/turn-by-turn.png)

#### Suggested directions

Just Ahead can also help you avoid getting lost by suggesting directions. Just Ahead tells you why you should turn or not, what you should do after a turn, and recommends the best direction to take if there are multiple route options. It’s like having a professional tour guide in the car with you.

* * *

###### Trip-planning resources

Every time we go on a trip, we stress out about when to go, where to stay, what to see, etc. Wouldn’t it be great if you had someone with you who had been on that exact trip countless times? Sharing tips and tricks before you even leave your house? Just Ahead does exactly that.

###### We get you there and back

Just Ahead tells you everything you need to know about your destination. But we also know that there are a lot of miles between home and the park, or between this park and the next. That’s why we cover all the common routes to and from your destination. No matter which route you choose, we’re with you, telling you stories along the way.

###### Where next?

We at Just Ahead are working to build the most comprehensive series of audio guides for the whole world. Wherever you’re traveling, we want to be there.

## We've handcrafted  your next scavenger hunt adventure

Let's Roam offers a diverse range
of scavenger hunt experiences to suit every occasion and interest. Choose from city exploration, bar crawls,
ghost tours, art walks, date night packages, and more. We're always adding new adventures to keep your curiosity
ignited.

![People on a scavenger hunt walking tour](https://www.letsroam.com/assets/images/letsroam/home_page/lr_home_video_thumbnail.jpg)

expert event planners are here to help you coordinate and host your event, whether it's for a few people or a
few thousand! Your get-together is about to get WAY more exciting.

markdown:
![Banner](https://geotourist.com/img/hero-mobile-discover.835077c8.svg)

# Experience your environment in a new and inspiring way

Discover the world around you or create your own immersive experiences

[Get started for free](https://geotourist.com/discover)

[![google play](https://geotourist.com/img/google-play-badge.7ff1be98.svg)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.geotourist.geotourist)[![app store](https://geotourist.com/img/app-store-badge.9633872f.svg)](https://apps.apple.com/ua/app/geotourist/id948290494)

How it Works

DiscoverCreate

![Pick your journey](https://geotourist.com/img/pick-journey.11e2d030.svg)

Pick your journey

Look for journeys nearby or from local experts around the world.

![Experience it](https://geotourist.com/img/experience-it.bbd14b33.svg)

Experience it

Pop headphones on and discover the world as never before

![Share and remix](https://geotourist.com/img/badge-share.bd60e1c1.svg)

Share and remix

Leave feedback, rate and remix, and make your own custom adventures

Features

### Walk and play

Build your own journeys and inspire others to follow in your footsteps. Your audio will trigger as they walk along your path, in an immersive experience like never before.

![walk and play](https://geotourist.com/img/walk-play.488a54c9.webp)

![better cities](https://geotourist.com/img/better-cities.81d48494.svg)

### Smarter cities

Immerse yourself in a world that comes alive as you roam, telling you their stories and connecting you with their communities. Enjoy discounts from local businesses, and book tickets to local events, along the routes – and avoid tourist traps.

### The Freedom to Discover

With tours available in over 40 languages and route mapping from your location, Geotourist gives you the confidence to explore and the freedom to discover stories all over the world.

![Age of Discovery](https://geotourist.com/img/age-of-discovery.cf66ebef.webp)

## Featured tours  ![search](https://geotourist.com/img/search.65fb7847.svg)

[![tour thumbnail](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/tours/photos/000/007/928/thumb_crop/data.jpg?1780057138)\\
\\
3.4 km  · 20 Points](https://geotourist.com/tours/7928/Maesteg_Town_Culture_and_Heritage_Trail)

[AUDIO TOUR\\
\\
Maesteg Town Culture and Heritage Trail](https://geotourist.com/tours/7928/Maesteg_Town_Culture_and_Heritage_Trail)

[Explore the culture and heritage of the town of Maesteg through the voices of local people. This is a walking tour around the town of Maesteg starting and ending at the Town Hall and has been put together with the help of local residents and businesses to give a true flavour of the aspects that are important to the people that live there. \\
\\
The Maesteg Town Culture and Heritage Trail was funded by Cardiff Metropolitan University in 2026 via the Research Wales Innovation Fund and was project managed by staff from the Welsh Centre for Tourism Research in the Cardiff School of Management and the Cardiff School of Education and Social Policy. It was narrated by Graham-Loveluck Edwards and curated by Jenny Hulme.](https://geotourist.com/tours/7928/Maesteg_Town_Culture_and_Heritage_Trail)

Bridgend County Borough Council 1,230

[![tour thumbnail](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/tours/photos/000/007/818/thumb_crop/the-hallmarked-man-reveal-landscape.jpg?1756292513)\\

Arizona Biltmore 8,606

[![tour thumbnail](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/tours/photos/000/003/612/thumb_crop/data.jpg?1580715174)\\
\\
Rated 5 stars out of 5\\
\\
770 km  · 42 Points](https://geotourist.com/tours/3612/VisitScotland_With_Outlander)

[AUDIO TOUR\\
\\
VisitScotland With Outlander](https://geotourist.com/tours/3612/VisitScotland_With_Outlander)

[Discover the locations behind the magic of the Outlander series with VisitScotland.\\
\\
If you’re a fan of Outlander, you’ll love discovering the TV locations - and some may be more surprising than you think!\\
\\
Delve into the world of clans and romance and explore the locations which featured in the hit TV series.\\
\\
From Castle Leoch to the North Carolina wilderness, use this guide to discover the sites that were used in filming and follow in Jamie and Claire’s footsteps for yourself.\\
\\
Outlander is available to watch now – check local listings for broadcaster details](https://geotourist.com/tours/3612/VisitScotland_With_Outlander)

VisitScotland 31,571

[![tour thumbnail](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/tours/photos/000/000/556/thumb_crop/data.jpg?1445529143)\\
\\
Rated 2 stars out of 5\\
\\
34 km  · 14 Points](https://geotourist.com/tours/556/Civil_War_Trail_of_Boyle_Co_Kentucky)

[AUDIO TOUR\\
\\
Civil War Trail of Boyle Co, Kentucky](https://geotourist.com/tours/556/Civil_War_Trail_of_Boyle_Co_Kentucky)

[Boyle County, like much of Kentucky, was politically divided during the Civil War. While most of Danville supported the Union, other pockets of the county backed the Confederacy. For example, the Rev. Robert J. Breckinridge was a Unionist leader in Danville, but two of his sons fought for the South.\\
\\
Boyle County was home to two Union generals, Speed Fry and Jeremiah Boyle. Fry was a hero of the Battle of Mill Springs, and Boyle, who became the commander of the Military District of Kentucky, was the son of Judge John Boyle, the county namesake.\\
\\
The largest battle on Kentucky soil was fought at Perryville, located in the northwest corner of Boyle County. This important battle, which was a turning point in the Civil War, kept Kentucky in Union hands for the remainder of the war. The battlefield and the town of Perryville still look much as they did in the 19th century.\\
\\
Boyle County experienced the horrors of the Civil War more than any other Kentucky county. Enduring several cavalry raids, a shootout in downtown, a guerilla raid, and the Commonwealth’s largest battle, residents were able to persevere and build a thriving community after the war.](https://geotourist.com/tours/556/Civil_War_Trail_of_Boyle_Co_Kentucky)

Destination Danville Ky 7,575

[![tour thumbnail](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/tours/photos/000/007/650/thumb_crop/data.jpg?1754062510)\\
\\
8.4 km  · 11 Points](https://geotourist.com/tours/7650/On_the_Map-_stories_from_Nether_Lochaber)

[AUDIO TOUR\\
\\
'On the Map'- stories from Nether Lochaber](https://geotourist.com/tours/7650/On_the_Map-_stories_from_Nether_Lochaber)

[Nether Lochaber is made up of a series of small villages and crofting townships on the eastern side of Loch Linnhe, stretching from the Ballachulish Bridge to just south of Fort William. As you will discover on this tour, the area offers hidden histories and surprising stories, as told by locals. \\
\\
This trail forms part of the 'Discover Nether Lochaber' interactive map, designed to help you discover the area by foot, bike, car, or even from your sofa. Explore the map using the link and discover cycling and walking routes, photos, 360° videos and more.\\
\\
The trail and map have been created as part of the 'On the Map' project, a collaboration between the Nether Lochaber Community Association and the University of the Highlands and Islands, with funding from Interface. \\
\\
Image: 1877 Ordnance Survey map. Reproduced with the permission of the National Library of Scotland CC-BY (NLS)](https://geotourist.com/tours/7650/On_the_Map-_stories_from_Nether_Lochaber)

## Red Nacional de Tours Autoguiados   en México

#### Conoce Centros Históricos, Pueblos Mágicos, Zonas Arqueológicas y Rutas Religiosas con audioguías culturales

### Explora México con Audioguías Culturales

Descubre zonas arqueológicas, pueblos mágicos y ciudades históricas con audioguías profesionales en varios idiomas.

[Explorar Audioguías](https://audioguiasmexicotour.com/catalogo)

![audioguias](https://audioguiasmexicotour.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/audioguiastourmexico-web-1024x577.png)

## Infraestructura Cultural Digital   para el Turismo en México

Audioguías a la Mexicana es una plataforma cultural diseñada para complementar la experiencia turística en destinos históricos, zonas arqueológicas y ciudades patrimoniales de México.

Nuestro sistema permite a visitantes nacionales e internacionales explorar el patrimonio cultural del país mediante audioguías autoguiadas accesibles desde su smartphone, disponibles en múltiples idiomas y sin necesidad de aplicaciones.

La plataforma está diseñada para integrarse fácilmente con sistemas de movilidad turística, aeropuertos, hoteles y destinos culturales, convirtiendo cada recorrido en una experiencia educativa e inmersiva.

**Disponible actualmente en zonas arqueológicas, centros históricos, pueblos mágicos y rutas culturales de México.**

### Elige tu propio ritmo

✔ La manera más hermosa de conocer un destino es “A Tour Paso”

✔ Concierge Digital 24/7 impulsado por IA

### Experiencias Personalizadas

✔ Sin grupos ni horarios fijos

✔ Más económico que un tour tradicional

### Ecosistema Cultural Completo

✔ Disponible en 4 idiomas

✔ Narrativa cultural profunda y profesional

### Tecnología Inmersiva

✔ IA conversacional contextual que adapta el contenido según ubicación e intereses.

✔ Audio premium multilingüe optimizado para una experiencia cultural envolvente.

### Todo el poder de la Inteligencia Artificial   en tus Audios con calidad Premium

#### Español

[Escuchar Bienvenida](https://audioguiasmexicotour.com/#elementor-action%3Aaction%3Dpopup%3Aopen%26settings%3DeyJpZCI6IjU0NTEiLCJ0b2dnbGUiOmZhbHNlfQ%3D%3D)

### “Somos una red nacional de inmersiones culturales digitales autoguiadas, diseñada para complementar el turismo presencial y ampliar el acceso al patrimonio.”

## Centros Históricos

Disfruta los principales Centros Históricos de México con tours autoguiados. Camina por plazas, catedrales y monumentos con narrativa cultural profesional desde tu smartphone.

[Explorar](https://audioguiasmexicotour.com/shop-2/swoof/product_cat-centros-historicos/)

iPhone

Experience the magic of GPS audio walks, cycles, drives and even boat rides with VoiceMap's self-guided tours in over 600 destinations worldwide.

VoiceMap tours are like podcasts that move with you, to tell stories about what you’re seeing right now. They're produced by insightful local storytellers, including journalists, filmmakers, novelists, podcasters, and tour guides. Ian McKellen has even created a tour. So have the Daily Show and Sir Stephen Fry.

Why use VoiceMap?

• Explore at your own pace instead of being herded along in a group. Start and stop tours whenever you like, to grab a drink or take in the view, then tap Resume to pick up exactly where you left off.
• Focus on your surroundings, not the screen. With automatic GPS playback, you can just tap on Start and let VoiceMap guide you.
• Avoid expensive roaming fees or fiddly connection issues. After you download a tour, VoiceMap works offline and includes an offline map.
• Enjoy tours as many times as you like, both in your destination and with your feet up, at home. Virtual Playback turns every tour into a podcast or audio book.
• Extend your attention span with indoor tours that help you make the most of your time at a growing range of museums and art galleries around the world.
• With over 2,100 free and paid tours in 80 countries, VoiceMap offers huge variety. There are over 100 tours in London alone!

- This was the third VoiceMap tour I’ve done and while the other two were excellent, this was my favorite. The author did a fabulous job of bringing the city to life through engaging stories and interesting comments. It is obvious she is passionate about the city. The tour takes you to various historical sites in a logical manner, starting and ending in the main downtown area. Pay attention to the directions while walking. They are detailed and will keep you on the right track and use the map only as a backup. The author brings history to life and explains the significance of Annapolis during the revolutionary war period as well as the contributions of enslaved people. Standing on the spot where Kunte Kinte was sold into slavery was chilling. I highly recommend this tour which takes only about an hour but is filled with so much information. After the tour we went back to explore some of the places mentioned in more detail. Going into the State House to see the room where George Washington submitted his resignation was a highlight. Actually reading his original letter with the markings and edits he made, forced me to reflect on this historical moment in our history. This tour will not disappoint. You can go at your own pace and not worry about keeping up with some tour guide or dealing with other patrons monopolizing the tour. Kudos to the author.

Also beware that to have the app running continuously over a long period is going to eat the phone battery. Carry an extended battery pack or charger just in case.





Developer Response



Hi there – You shouldn't lose a download if you close the app. Did you sign out of your VoiceMap account maybe? If you do that, then yes, tours on the device are deleted – but this is because we assume that you're signing out to allow you or somebody else to sign in with a different account, and that second account shouldn't have access to the same tours. If you don't sign out, this won't be a problem. Just end the tour and then use the Resume option instead. The app doesn't track your location if you are either browsing the tour or actually doing one, and as a result it won't drain your battery.

- This update marks the biggest aesthetic change to VoiceMap in twelve years. We've replaced our old literal icon, of headphones on a pin, with something more figurative – a red dot embraced by a winding route.

The app's interface has also been refreshed, to help you choose between our growing catalogue of tours. There are well over 2,000 now, with new tours published every day by a community of close to 800 publishers.

We're introducing two of them with this release:

• Stephen Fry has reunited with the QI Elves to produce two Quite Interesting tours of London. You'll find all the wild tangents, nerdy footnotes and remarkable facts that you'd expect from one of the UK's most entertaining and intelligent panel shows.
• History Hit, who make some of the world's most popular history podcasts, join us with two tours narrated by their founder Dan Snow. One follows the Great Fire that reshaped this great city. The other tells the story of Charles I, executed in front of his own palace.

The new icon is a symbol of what we think VoiceMap has become: not just audio files pinned to a map, but an invitation to a more engaged, more meaningful kind of travel and a celebration of the curiously human details that make us feel like insiders, wherever we are – or wherever we go to next.

- VoiceMap published its 2,026th tour in the first week of 2026 – and that number has gone up almost every day since. Our latest additions open up the new destinations of Livigno and Cortina d'Ampezzo. There's a new option in Milan too, specifically about the Winter Olympics, so we're using that as the codename for Version 15 of the app. Welcome to VoiceMap Milan! Here's what you'll find:

• 50 odd categories, from Architecture and Medieval History to Ghosts and Hauntings, Food and Drink, Crime and Mystery. Browse them on the home screen, use them to filter tours in a destination, or combine them with filters for distance and rating. Some categories span hundreds of tours. Others cover a handful – the kind of niche, personal tours that only a platform with nearly 800 publishers can offer.
• Tour passes for a single destination, a whole country, or the entire VoiceMap catalogue. With passes, the cost per tour drops considerably, but every tour you choose stays in your library forever.
• While our goal is to make following a tour so easy that you never really need to look at the map, from start to finish, we've now added numbered locations you can toggle on and off as you walk – especially when the app suspects you've gone off track and Ian McKellen chimes in with, "Not all who wander are lost, but it looks like you might be".
• A rethought fallback start option that lets you begin a tour from anywhere along its route with numbered locations enabled by default.
• Labels that indicate when a tour was produced with significant use of AI, whether that's for the script itself, the voiceover, or for translation. We hope VoiceMap as a whole stands for authentic, curiously human tours with insight from very real people, and it's because of this that we think it's important to note where a publisher has leaned on an AI tool.

Autio - Audio for Travel
\\*\\*\\* Apple App of the Day, Apps We Love, & New & Noteworthy
\\*\\*\\* Webby Award Winner for Best Travel App

Ready to take travel to the next level? Autio has 20,000+ location-based audio stories in America and around the world. Try your first 5 stories free - no strings attached - then choose a plan for 30 Days, 1 Year, or 3 Years.

Ever curious about the deeper story behind that bronze historical marker you passed on the highway? Autio is an invitation to discover — a hands-free experience that delights, informs, & entertains by fostering a deeper connection with the people, places, & histories of the land you are traveling through.

With rave reviews from Forbes, Travel & Leisure, The New York Times, Outside, TechCrunch, & more!

FEATURES:

NARRATED BY YOUR FAVORITE VOICES — Many of our stories are narrated by voices you know and love like Kevin Costner, Phil Jackson, John Lithgow, and more.

DISCOVER INTERESTING STORIES — Autio notifies you when you’re in range of new stories you haven’t heard yet.

ALWAYS SOMETHING NEW — New stories are released weekly, so no two trips are ever the same.

GROWING COVERAGE — Unique stories from across America and beyond.

FOCUS ON WHAT MATTERS — Audio stories keep your eyes off your phone and on your beautiful surroundings.

HOW IT WORKS

As you travel, Autio serves up stories based on your geographic location & interests. The audio vignettes, generally 2-3 minutes in length, tell the history around you, painting a multi-dimensional picture you’re unlikely to get from a history book or visitor's guide. Autio answers the questions we all ask as the odometer turns.

ABOUT AUTIO

Humans are moved by stories. Stories that make us laugh and cry. They move us to come together and do amazing things. Since the dawn of time, stories have been the way in which values and knowledge are passed from one generation to the next — each adding their wisdom and experience along the way.

It’s time to connect with the sum of our experience, to enrich our lives with the stories of today, and to inspire the great storytellers yet to come.

iPhone, iPad

Uncover the hidden history right beneath your feet.

On This Spot is your ultimate interactive companion for deep historical exploration. Whether you are walking through your local downtown, planning a road trip, or exploring from home, we bring the past into the present through immersive multimedia storytelling, guided tours, and interactive tools and games.

Deep Historical Tours: Follow expert-curated paths through cities, regional heritage sites, and iconic routes.

Rich Audio & Video Content: Don't just read about history—hear the stories come alive and watch archival moments unfold through integrated multimedia.

Interactive Scavenger Hunts: Turn exploration into an adventure. Challenge yourself with photo restaging, timeline puzzles, trivia, and augmented reality (AR) experiences that reveal the secrets of the past.

Stunning "Then & Now" Photography: View thousands of historic photos precisely mapped to the exact spot they were taken. Use our advanced camera engine to align, shot-match, and create your own seamless past-meets-present photo mashups.

Hundreds of Destinations Across North America & Europe

Western Canada: Vancouver, Victoria, Calgary, Edmonton, Saskatoon, Banff, Jasper, Revelstoke, the Okanagan, and dozens of heritage towns across BC and Alberta.
Eastern Canada: Toronto, Montreal, Ottawa, Quebec City, Halifax, Charlottetown, St. John's, Niagara Falls, and regional heritage counties.
United Kingdom & Europe: London, Manchester, Liverpool, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Cardiff, Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt, and historic WWII sites including Dieppe, Juno Beach, and Omaha Beach.
International Landmarks: Washington DC, Chichen Itza, and much more.

Download On This Spot today!

iPhone, iPad

Turn your city into a game.

Questo is an outdoor escape game, scavenger hunt, and self-guided walking tour in one app. Over 1 million players. Rated 4.7 stars. Playable in 1,000+ cities worldwide.

Need a date-night idea, a weekend activity with the kids, or a fresh way to see a city you love? Put the phone between you and the streets, and the real world becomes your playground.

TWO WAYS TO PLAY

1\. Outdoor escape games (for locals)
Spontaneous adventures in your own city. Like an escape room, but outdoors.
• For couples: "Murder Mystery: Crime on Date Night." Skip dinner and a movie and team up to catch a killer.
• For families: "Kid Quest," made for ages 4 to 8. Walk the park, solve easy riddles, take photos together.
• For friends: race to crack the case before time runs out.

2\. Story-driven tours (for travelers)
Don't just look at landmarks. Step into the story behind them. Local writers turn history and legend into walking games.
• New York: "Hamilton." London: "Jack the Ripper." Zurich: "Einstein." Paris: "Lost Lovers in Montmartre."
• And new adventures: "Murder Mystery Zodiac," "The 9 Lives Heist," and "The Lost Gold."

MORE THAN READING, IT'S PLAYING
Questo isn't a text walk. It's interactive.
• Puzzles that use your phone and your senses, like blowing on the screen to clear the dust and reveal the next clue.
• Video woven into the story, so you watch history come alive instead of just reading about it.
• Time Rifts: see how the place you're standing looked centuries ago.
• Every quest reshapes the app to match its world.

PLAY TOGETHER
• Co-op: share one phone and solve as a team.
• Versus: split into teams and race. The leaderboard shows who's fastest.
• Crews: join or start a group, play together, and compete for the top spot.

KEEP THE MEMORIES
• Memories: after you finish, re-read every story and relive the quest.
• Explorer Photos: see real photos from other players, and share your own.

PLAY IN YOUR LANGUAGE
Quests in multiple languages, many with an audio version so you can listen as you walk.

HOW IT WORKS

Download and browse the map to find a game near you.
Head to the starting point. No schedule, start whenever your group is ready.
Use the statues, buildings, and street art around you to solve riddles and unlock the next part of the story.

WHY QUESTO
• Real connection: put the screens down and be with the people around you.
• Budget friendly: far less than an escape room or a guided tour.
• Flexible: pause for lunch or a coffee anytime.
• Gift it: buy a quest for someone you love.

Ready to play? Download Questo and turn your next walk into an adventure.

Because Clio is free, it depends upon people like you who care about history and culture. If you would like to help, please send us an email at clio@theclio.com We are working to provide new features like push notifications and interactive walking tours thanks to donations and other forms of support. The Clio Foundation is recognized as a public charity under IRS code 501c3 and all donations are tax deductible.

With several hundred new entries and improvements being added each month, Clio is not only a website and smartphone application, but also a collaborative research, interpretation, and map-building project. Museum professionals, scholars, and their students contribute most of Clio’s content. We also depend upon local history experts and museum volunteers who often know more about local history than anyone else. Each day, this partnership of local history experts and professional historians is building a comprehensive, dynamic, and interactive map of American history.

The biggest issue was with the amount of content. There were only 10 “stops” on the tour. One of them was city hall which isn’t in Little Tokyo. At least two of the stops were just updates that you were going in the right direction. So, really, only 7 stops on the tour. The information was good but for FIFTEEN DOLLARS I was expecting a lot more. There is a lot to see in Little Tokyo and this tour barely scratched the surface. Not worth the money.

- We tried to use the app to take a “peaceful” driving tour through Sedona. The app failed to integrate to our car’s information center, but I won’t blame that on the app, since I’m not 100% sure. The directions were hard to follow. When we tried to restart the tour on a site other than the first one, she got wrapped around the axle and kept repeating the introduction multiple times. We ended up closing the app and giving up. Wish we could get our money back. The narrator’s voice was nice.

Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. We're truly sorry to hear about your experience while using our app in Sedona, and can completely understand your frustration. We’ll look into how the app handles resuming from a different site, and the repeating introduction you encountered is something we’ll work on fixing.I also want to apologize for any inconvenience caused by the lack of integration with your car’s information center. We're continuously working to ensure our app is compatible with as many systems as possible.If you’re open to it, we’d love to make it up to you. Please feel free to reach out to us directly at support@ucplaces.com, and we’d be happy to offer you a refund or help you find another tour experience that better meets your expectations. We appreciate your kind words about the narrator’s voice and hope we can provide you with a more seamless experience in the future!

iPhone, iPad

Why go on a boring old walk when you can be a secret agent? Or run through the streets of a new city to escape a zombie apocalypse? Have you ever read a story and wished you could be in it? Calling the shots, helping the good guys (or bad), choosing your adventure. Story City makes you the hero of your own story, giving you the chance to take part in your own adventure in cities across the world.

Each story only opens when you're in the right location. Whether it's fiction or non-fiction, a musical journey or scavenger hunt, all stories on Story City are made by creators who know their cities best.

Interested in a story you can't get to because of travel restrictions (or money restrictions!)? Then why not check out our creators' award-winning adventures from the comfort of your home via spoiler mode?

Each story starts at a particular location in the city it’s set and can either follow one path or branch off into dozens of different locations around the city (and which ones you visit will depend on the path you pick through the adventure).

Will you explore Atlanta while running from a zombie apocalypse? Or how about cruising the Austin streets while solving a mystery? Or will you be pillaging the city looking for pirate supplies? Perhaps you'll take a musical journey with a Native American storyteller and drummer, or learn about your local non-profit in a social issues walk.

It’s your adventure, so it’s up to you!

The world is full of adventures. Choose yours.

IMPORTANT - Story City uses background GPS, to ensure story pages are unlocked when you reach the target location. If you turn off the functionality, the app will cease to work. Please see Story City website help pages for information on how to turn the GPS back on if you have accidentally turned it off.

Continued use of GPS running in the background can dramatically decrease battery life. We recommend the use of a battery pack while playing.

At the southwestern corner of mainland British Columbia, the land around what would become Vancouver has been inhabited by First Nations peoples for thousands of years.

The first European settlers arrived in the 1860s and erected sawmills to begin clearing the thick evergreen forests around Vancouver's deep harbour. In 1886 the town was made the western terminus of the Canadian Pacific Railway and the city began a massive building boom, which was not hindered by the devastating Great Fire that same year.

Vancouver quickly became the economic metropolis for British Columbia's vast resource-rich hinterland. Today the city is the economic and cultural heart of the province, and over half of British Columbians live in and around Vancouver.

## Off to the Klondike

* * *

![Off to the Klondike](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/kerfooto.jpg)![Off to the Klondike](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/kerfootn.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM54-S4-: Str P336](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/big-outfit-starting-for-klondike-in-front-of-johnston-kerfoot-and-company-104-and-106-cordova-street-vancouver-b-c)

1898

A huge crowd has assembled in front of Johnston and Kerfoot's Klondike Outfitters to see a mule train equipped for the arduous journey to the gold fields. As tens of thousands of American prospectors made their way north, the prohibitive customs duties on bringing supplies across the border meant that most stopped in Vancouver to kit out. As a result the gold rush was a huge economic boon for Vancouver and marked the start of Vancouver's most dizzying expansion which would last until 1913.

## The Seven Sisters

* * *

![The Seven Sisters](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/sevensisters2o.jpg)![The Seven Sisters](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/sevensisters2n.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM54-S4-: St Pk P76.2](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/seven-sisters-stanley-park-vancouver-b-c)

1920s

The trees that once grew from these stumps were called the Seven Sisters. The six douglas firs and a red cedar were thought to be over 700 years old and from the park's earliest days they impressed visitors with their magnificent size. The iconic Canadian poet Pauline Johnson called them the "Cathedral trees" and said "There is no fresco that can rival the delicacy of lace-work they have festooned between you and the far skies." There are several stories about how they got their name. According to one, published in an article in the Vancouver Daily Province in 1949, when Lord Stanley opened Stanley Park in 1889 there were only seven girls between the ages of 10 and 18 in the city's 1,000 odd residents, and this was their favourite spot to play. Hence the Seven Sisters. By the 1960s they had died, and it was feared they would fall and injure someone so they were cut down.

A number of prominent buildings are visible, such as the second Hotel Vancouver (far right, now demolished), the Vancouver block (with the white clock tower at right), the Birks Block (just in front of the Vancouver Block, now demolished) and the Post Office (centre right, above the steamship docks).

## Ships Passing at Sunset

* * *

![Ships Passing at Sunset](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/prospectpointsunseto.jpg)![Ships Passing at Sunset](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/prospectpointsunsetn.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM54-S4-2-: CVA 371-1462](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/view-at-sunset-from-prospect-point-across-burrard-inlet-towards-west-vancouver)

1930s

Two ships pass each other at the entrance to Vancouver harbour in this rather moody shot from the 1930s.

## Crossing the Bridge

* * *

![Crossing the Bridge](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/bridgeopening3o.jpg)![Crossing the Bridge](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/bridgeopening3n.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM1535-: CVA 99-2656](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/opening-of-burrard-bridge-10)

1932

Crowds walk across the freshly completed Burrard Street Bridge for the first time. The bridge is fairly unique for the Art Deco design of the superstructure, a style of building that flourished in the 1920s and 1930s that sought to combine modern technology and science with careful attention to detail and beauty. You can learn more about Art Deco in the Architecture Tour.

## Ferrara Court

* * *

![Ferrara Court](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/hastingsjacksono.jpg)![Ferrara Court](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/hastingsjacksonn.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM54-S4-1---: CVA 20-52](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/hastings-street-and-jackson-avenue-southeast-city)

1932

This photo gives a look at the many advertisements always present in Vancouver. The most common advertisements in old photos by far are for cigarettes and real estate agents. The second building at the left has an ad for MILLBANK Virginia Cigarettes.

## Building the Lions Gate

* * *

![Building the Lions Gate](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/buildinglionsgateo.jpg)![Building the Lions Gate](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/buildinglionsgaten.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM54-S4-: Br P81.26](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/view-of-lions-gate-bridge-under-construction-3)

1938

Work is beginning on installing the bridge deck on the Lions Gate bridge.

## Industrial Operations

* * *

![Industrial Operations](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/cityhallbackgroundo.jpg)![Industrial Operations](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/cityhallbackgroundn.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM640-S1-: CVA 260-1040](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/unidentified-mill-on-false-creek-2)

1939

A sawmill belches smoke on a tranquil looking False Creek. It is evident that this stands where the casino stands today because the new city hall on Cambie can be seen dominating the skyline in the background. Today it is partially obscured by the growing number of condo towers, though they are both lined up.

## Captain Vancouver

* * *

![Captain Vancouver](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/captainvancouverstatueo.jpg)![Captain Vancouver](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/captainvancouverstatuen.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM1545-S3-: CVA 586-164](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/captain-vancouver-statue-looking-over-van-couver-from-city-hall)

1940

The statue of Captain George Vancouver looks out over the city that bears his name. He would probably be quite pleased at this outcome, as his name was only picked after Gastown and then Granville were thought unsuitable. It was actually CPR President Van Horne who suggested the name. Granville, a former colonial secretary, didn't have the same ring to it as the intrepid explorer whose voyages to the Pacific were known to every school-child in Britain. Van Horne wanted a name people would remember and advertise the city. Since the CPR basically controlled the city, Van Horne got his way.

## Court House From Robson

* * *

![Court House From Robson](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/courthousehotelo.jpg)![Court House From Robson](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/courthousehoteln.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM1545-S3-: CVA 586-4159](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/view-of-western-photo-building-and-surrounding-buildings-from-robson-street-and-granville-street)

1945

The courthouse, now the art gallery, and beyond it the Hotel Vancouver, can be seen in this foggy photo taken from Robson Street.

## Homecoming Parade

* * *

![Homecoming Parade](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/homecomingo.jpg)![Homecoming Parade](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/homecomingn.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives AM1545-S3-: CVA 586-4035](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/seaforth-highlanders-homecoming-parade-on-georgia-street)

1945

The Seaforth Highlanders march past a reviewing stand in front of the Hotel Georgia to celebrate their return from Europe at the end of the Second World War.

## Granville Strip in the 60s

* * *

![Granville Strip in the 60s](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/daytimetheatreso.jpg)![Granville Strip in the 60s](https://onthisspot.ca/app/vancouver/big/daytimetheatresn.jpg)

Fade

[Vancouver Archives COV-S511---: CVA 780-55](https://searcharchives.vancouver.ca/view-of-granville-street-theatre-row)

1967

A busy Granville strip and so-called Theatre Row. Standing at the same spot today you'll see how little has changed in the last 60 years, save the makes of the cars and the fashion choices of the pedestrians.

## Frequently asked questions

What can I do in New York City with Questo?

Browse outdoor city games built around New York City. Each quest has its own route and story: follow clues, solve puzzles, and discover the city as you play.

How many outdoor city games are available in New York City?

Questo currently lists 52 outdoor city games in New York City. Browse the collection to compare stories, routes, and access options.

Is there a murder mystery game in New York City?

Yes. Questo has murder mystery quests set on the real streets of New York City: follow the clues, question the evidence, and solve the case at your own pace. No actors, no booking, start whenever you like.

Is there a ghost tour in New York City?

Yes. Questo's self-guided ghost tours lead you to New York City's haunted places while you follow clues and uncover the dark stories behind them. Play any evening, no guide needed.

Do I need to book an activity in New York City in advance?

Discover New York City through Questo's outdoor city games. Follow clues through the streets of Manhattan, across Brooklyn Bridge, and into the neighborhoods that make NYC unlike anywhere else. Murder mysteries, hidden history, and stories behind every block, all on your phone, at your own pace. No guide, no group, no schedule.

### About New York City

New York City holds more stories per block than most cities hold per borough. Questo gives you a way into those stories: phone in hand, clues on screen, and a self-guided city game that turns any afternoon into an actual adventure.

The city splits into neighborhoods that feel like separate worlds. Central Park sits at the geographic and emotional center of Manhattan, ringed by landmarks like Bethesda Terrace and Belvedere Castle. Downtown, Greenwich Village keeps its reputation for brownstone-lined streets, independent energy, and Washington Square Park as a communal front yard. Brooklyn adds a different rhythm entirely, with street art corridors and a pace that rewards wandering.

Questo's 32 original quests across the city cover a wide range of moods. There are mystery-driven games for those who want to uncover hidden histories, romantic routes through Central Park designed for couples, supernatural storylines set in the oldest corners of Manhattan, and pop-culture adventures through Midtown. Families, solo explorers, and friend groups each find something that fits.

A few things worth knowing before you go: New York City rewards walking by neighborhood rather than jumping between boroughs in a single day. Group your quests by area and let yourself slow down between stops. The subway map compresses real distances, so what looks like a short hop can be a 20-minute walk above ground.

Questo's New York City quests are rated 4.56★ across 302 player reviews. Choose a quest, pick your neighborhood, and let the city surprise you.

## How the VoiceMap app works

- Focus on your surroundings, not the screen



The VoiceMap app uses GPS to play audio automatically, at the right time and place, so you can focus on your surroundings, not the screen.



![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/routes/how_vm_works/item-1-2edf87afb83357cd9c9d206dfd3ffe6c81922b253b523cb78761b5bd4553be62.webp)

- Follow a route with turn-by-turn-directions



VoiceMap tours follow a route from a fixed starting point. That lets us give turn-by-turn directions and use context to tell a better story.



![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/routes/how_vm_works/item-2-6cdcd7de34743f0fa9f492553420f3974107f0d7e857e5ca715e982d50fd739b.webp)

- Resume playback to go at your own pace



If you'd like to stop for a drink or go into a museum, end your tour then use the Resume feature to pick up exactly where you left off.



![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/routes/how_vm_works/item-3-587ebe4cfc56ddae9017f4a545a2dac13a44f13c82dc5527e9bb27108fe8184d.webp)

- Listen as many times as you like



You can listen to your tours as often as you like using both the VoiceMap app and website.



![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/routes/how_vm_works/item-4-3695a55dad2b1f0481089eddbb1fad32c516081842d18a84431264a68d96016e.webp)

- Take virtual tours anywhere, like a podcast



Select Virtual mode in the VoiceMap app to listen to tours like a podcast - at home or in transit.



![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/routes/how_vm_works/item-5-eca17db9357c3cc183de9c78591bca79e8efa07aa500c928bb908538fd0fb941.webp)

- Buy for less on voicemap.me and sync



Once you've purchased a tour, it's added to your VoiceMap library. To access it in the app, just sign in using the same account.



![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/routes/how_vm_works/item-6-6e380f3a13ce24190f98e8049192a21d1b922552283cb2f2ef1b73a11a7d8dc2.webp)

Welcome to Downtown Montreal Welcome to Downtown Montreal! At the light, turn right on René-Lévesque Boulevard. As you drive through these bustling streets, you'll quickly notice that Montreal feels different from most North American cities. The elegant stone buildings, sidewalk cafés, and frequent French signs often make visitors feel as though they've crossed the Atlantic into Europe. Montreal is the largest French-speaking city in the Americas and one of the world's most bilingual metropolitan areas. While French is the official language of Quebec and the language you'll see on street signs and hear most often, English is also widely spoken, creating a unique blend of cultures that has shaped the city's identity for centuries. The city itself sits on an island between the mighty Saint Lawrence and Ottawa Rivers. It was founded by French settlers in 1642 as Ville-Marie, a small missionary colony. Over the centuries, Montreal grew into one of North America's most important ports and commercial centers, welcoming immigrants from around the world who added their own traditions, cuisines, and neighborhoods to its rich cultural tapestry. Today, more than four million people call the greater Montreal area home. It's a city celebrated for its world-class festivals, renowned restaurants, thriving arts scene, and passion for sports—especially hockey, which many locals consider more than just a game. As we explore, you'll discover that every neighborhood has its own personality. From sleek skyscrapers and historic churches to lively markets, Olympic landmarks, and charming waterfront streets, Montreal is a city of remarkable contrasts. So settle in and enjoy the drive as we begin discovering one of North America's most captivating destinations. Read More [https://www.mtl.org/en/what-to-do/neighbourhoods/downtown](https://www.mtl.org/en/what-to-do/neighbourhoods/downtown) Place #2 Distance: 0.21mi , Attraction : Skyscraper (Recommended selfie spot). ![Map Pin](https://ucplaces.com/public/images/map-pin.svg) ##### 625 Boul. René-Lévesque Ouest, Montréal, QC H3B 1R2, Canada ![POI 2 Tour Image](https://ucplaces.com/storage/app/public/tours/2794/point/2.jpg) UCPlaces self guided tour Audio Player 00:00 00:00 00:00 Use Up/Down Arrow keys to increase or decrease volume. Place Ville Marie - Iconic Cross-Shaped Tower Coming up on your right is Place Ville Marie, one of Montreal's most recognizable landmarks and a symbol of the city's modern transformation. Completed in 1962, this striking cruciform, or cross-shaped, skyscraper was the centerpiece of an ambitious redevelopment project that helped shift Montreal's commercial heart from Old Montreal to the downtown district you see today. At 47 stories tall, it was Canada's tallest building when it opened and quickly became an icon of progress and innovation. Place Ville Marie is far more than an office tower. Beneath your feet lies a vast underground network known as the RESO, or Underground City. Stretching for more than 30 kilometers, this remarkable system connects shopping centers, office buildings, hotels, metro stations, restaurants, and entertainment venues. During Montreal's long winters, hundreds of thousands of people use it daily to move comfortably around the city without stepping outside. If you look toward the top of the building, you may notice the large illuminated beacon that shines each night. It has become a familiar feature of Montreal's skyline and can be seen from miles away. For one of the city's best panoramic views, visitors can head to the Place Ville Marie observation terrace, offering spectacular vistas of downtown, Mount Royal, the Saint Lawrence River, and, on a clear day, far beyond the city limits. As we continue our journey, you'll see how this modern business district blends seamlessly with Montreal's historic roots, creating one of North America's most distinctive urban landscapes. Download the app ( [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ucplaces.app) or [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ucplaces/id1424277513)), purchase the tour (either here on the website, or from within the app). That's it, you're ready to go! When you want to start the tour, find the tour in the app (via a quick in-app search or by clicking the tour link received in your confirmation email) and click "Start Tour" (headphones recommended for best experience.) \\* After purchasing a tour you will receive a purchase confirmation email including the tour link and instructions on how to take the tour, so you don't have to remember anything now. How does the tour work? UCPlaces acts as your personal tour guide, providing self-guided audio tours fully navigated within our app using GPS-based navigation. You won't need to switch between external navigation apps. Whenever you approach a point of interest (POI) on the tour, our app will automatically play the relevant audio story at the right time and place. If you start the tour before reaching the first POI, the app will navigate you to the starting point and then begin the tour. How is this more convenient than a traditional tour? UCPlaces offers an innovative and flexible way to explore exciting destinations on your terms. Here are some key advantages over traditional tours: - No need to commit upfront or purchase in advance; buy a tour only when you're ready to go. - Walk at your own pace. - No waiting for groups; go on your schedule. - Take the tour in your preferred language. - Start, stop and continue the tour whenever you want. - Returning to the same destination? Take the tour again, and again, and again... And bring a friend! - Enjoy preferred prices. What's included? - A self-guided audio tour taken via the UCPlaces app \[iOS (iPhone) / Apple CarPlay / Android / Android Auto\]. - Tour route map and in-app GPS navigation (via the UCPlaces app). - Audio stories for places visited during the tour. - Apple CarPlay connection (iOS users) and Android Auto connection (Android users); for a seamless driving tour experience. What's NOT included? - Earphones (highly recommended). - Smartphone. - Any kind of transportation (including tickets and passes). - Tickets to the attractions on your tour. - Food and drinks - Physical tour guide. ### Have any questions about this tour? Or a general travel / self-guided tours question? That's completely natural + How long does this tour take? Most travelers complete this tour in approximately 2 to 3 hours, depending on pace, time spent at each stop, and optional detours. Having said that, please remember that self-guided tours are extremly flexible (you can start, pause, continue anytime) and everyone has their own pace. + What does this tour include? This self-guided driving tour includes 32 stops, covering top attractions such as Welcome to Downtown Montreal, Place Ville Marie - Iconic Cross-Shaped Tower, Mary, Queen of the World Cathedral, Dorchester Square, Boulevard René-Lévesque. + Where does the tour start? The tour starts at Welcome to Downtown Montreal (Address: 1205 Rue St-Alexandre, Montreal, QC H3B 3H5, Canada). You can begin the tour there or join from any stop along the route. + What type of tour is this? This is a self-guided driving tour designed to be completed by car, covering scenic routes, city highlights and optional key stops. + Can I do this tour at my own pace? Yes, this is a self-guided driving tour, so you can start anytime and explore at your own pace. You can pause, skip stops, or spend more time at places that interest you. You can even split it into multiple days. Explore however feels right for you. The only vaiables that might affect your pace are speed limits and traffic congestion. + Do I need a car for this tour? Yes, this is a driving tour, designed to be completed by car, with stops spread across different locations connected by a driving route. + Do I need anything in order to take the tour? There are two things that you need - 1. A mobile phone (with the UCPlaces app installed and active location services, and a cellular data plan with a decent signal for downloading the tour). 2. A car. Here are some recommendations for a great experience: 1. Make sure your phone is fully charged and bring a charging cable for your car. 2. Connect your phone to the car speaker system via bluetooth or use our CarPlay/Android Auto option for the best experience. + How will I navigate from point to point during the tour? The tour uses GPS-based navigation through the UCPlaces app, with automatic audio playback and step-by-step directions between stops. This works great either directly from your phone, or while connected to your car's multimedia system and using our CarPlay or Android Auto options. Just follow the route and listen to the audio guide. Use the resume feature to continue from where you recently stopped (or closed the app). Easily skip or go back to stops. + Is this tour suitable for families or groups? Yes, self-guided tours are ideal for families and small groups, allowing everyone to explore comfortably without being tied to a fixed schedule. + What makes a self-guided tour better than a guided tour? Self-guided tours are more flexible, affordable, and personalized. You can avoid crowds, choose your pace, and focus on the stops that interest you most. + I installed the app and it's now asking for GPS and media access permissions, why? The app is your tour-guide, it needs to know where you are located on the map to be able to trigger the points of interest. It also needs access to audio and media files to provide you with this experience. + What happens if there are unexpected roadblocks or navigation issues? We have been working hard to deliver a great experience. Though you may run into unexpected obstacles (the world is constantly changing), our app has multiple features and mechanisms in place to help you overcome them, including: AI assistance, force play an audio if you can't reach the stop, skip or return to stops, automatic rerouting and more. + Can I take the tour in my language? Though all of our tours are primarily in English, many tours are muyltilingual (including: Spanish, German, Portuguese, French, Japanese, Hebrew, French, Arabic and more...). The tour language options depend on the specific tour - You can easily check which languages are available in the tour screen! ✕ - Welcome to UCPlaces! ### Arizona Biltmore History Tour

1.2 km · Aug 2015

United States

Frank-Lloyd-Wright, Phoenix, McArthur, Hotel, Navajo, Waldorf-Astoria, William-Wrigley-Jnr., golf, Marilyn-Monroe, Arizona-Canal, United States

English

Rated 0 stars out of 5

0 Stars

0Reviews

8,607Views

A favorite vacation retreat of U.S. presidents and legendary film stars since 1929, Arizona Biltmore is one of the few hotels with an architectural imprint left by renowned American architect, Frank Lloyd Wright.

[![](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/tours/photos/000/000/401/thumb/data.jpg?1452627356)\\
\\
TOUR AUTHORArizona Biltmore](https://geotourist.com/user/232/Arizona_Biltmore) Follow

[![category](https://geotourist.com/img/12.f2d323b6.svg)Food](https://geotourist.com/discover?local=false&categories=12) [![category](https://geotourist.com/img/10.3827c63e.svg)City tour](https://geotourist.com/discover?local=false&categories=10) [![category](https://geotourist.com/img/5.94eada27.svg)Heritage](https://geotourist.com/discover?local=false&categories=5) [![category](https://geotourist.com/img/2.d1970a39.svg)Walking](https://geotourist.com/discover?local=false&categories=2) [![category](https://geotourist.com/img/1.7e788e8e.svg)Other](https://geotourist.com/discover?local=false&categories=1)

Share via

![link icon](https://geotourist.com/img/link.13a1aa31.svg)

[Tour Points 11 Points](https://geotourist.com/tours/401/point)

Start Tour

Explore At Home

![point](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/points/photos/000/001/039/thumb_crop/data.jpg?1439229637)![pin](https://geotourist.com/img/point-pin.b715ed0f.svg)1

[Arizona Biltmore History\\
\\
The story of Arizona Biltmore started when 2 brothers – Warren and Charles McArthur – moved from Chicago to Phoenix. Warren moved here in 1910 for health reasons, and his brother followed in 1913. Known for their entrepreneurial spirits, their first venture was a Dodge car dealership. Forever looking for the next “great idea” they didn’t stop with selling cars. They took one of their Dodge trucks and outfitted it with additional seats and a supply car. Their newest invention – called “The Wonderbus” was a hit as they took people on tours of the Arizona sites. By 1924, the brothers formed a vision of Arizona as a tourist destination lacking only their guidance and proper accommodations. \\
\\
In 1927 the brothers secured an agreement with the Bowman – Biltmore Hotel Group, and formed the Arizona Biltmore Corporation. They also convinced their brother – Albert Chase McArthur – an architect studying under Frank Lloyd Wright, to head the project. They secured the $1 million in capital to build the resort with the help of investors such as William Wrigley Jr, the chewing gum magnate. The land was secured 8 miles outside of Phoenix, in the foothills of Squaw Peak.\\
\\
Albert Chase McArthur’s design of the Biltmore would pay tribute to Frank Lloyd Wright’s architectural philosophy of organic architecture – using materials that are native to the site. With that in mind, McArthur chose to use the block construction technique Frank Lloyd Wright had used for homes he built in California. McArthur wrote Frank Lloyd Wright requesting permission to use the textile block system. In response, Wright requested a fee of $10,000, for not only the patent, but also to personally oversee the construction. Wright was invited to consult on the project and arrived onsite in January of 1928 and stayed for six, tension filled months. Unfortunately, after it was revealed that there was no legal patent, the relationship ended with the McArthur’s asking Wright and his family to leave the job site and their home.\\
\\
During the construction, a temporary block factory was set up to make the more than 250,000 blocks needed for the site. Again, using the organic philosophy, they used the sand onsite, and water from the Arizona canal to make the blocks. \\
\\
The design on the block has become a signature of the hotel. McArthur wanted the blocks to be decorative as well as functional. There are several interpretations as to what the design represents. Some say it’s the underside of a freshly cut palm tree, others say it was actually a representation of a mathematical equation for the refraction of light.](https://geotourist.com/tours/401/Arizona_Biltmore_History_Tour/point/1039/Arizona_Biltmore_History)

![point](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/points/photos/000/001/040/thumb_crop/data.jpg?1439229751)![pin](https://geotourist.com/img/point-pin.b715ed0f.svg)2

[Aztec Room\\
\\
Construction on the resort started in August 1928 and was finished in 9 months by February 1929. By the end, the building consisted of over 250,000 blocks, 33,000 pounds of copper in the roof. The building has the 2nd largest gold leaf ceiling in the world, only behind the Taj Mahal. \\
\\
On February 23, 1929 the resort opened in grand fashion. The resort had to re-create the opening gala three days in a row to accommodate the huge demand for the opening. With Wrigley at the helm, the Arizona Biltmore became the destination of choice for the Presidents, the rich, famous, and dignitaries from around the world. This became an invitation only resort and every year the Wrigley family would send out invitations to stay at the resort. \\
\\
The Aztec Room was built as the resort’s original ballroom. Wrigley did use this as a ballroom, but on Friday nights he turned it into a movie theater for his guests. If you look at the back wall and count 4 blocks in on the top, you may notice that the blocks are on hinges. That is actually where the reel-to-reel was kept. Senator McCain and Supreme Court Justice Sandra Day O’Connor both had their weddings in this room. President Regan and his wife Nancy honeymooned at the resort and had a party in this room.](https://geotourist.com/tours/401/Arizona_Biltmore_History_Tour/point/1040/Aztec_Room)

![point](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/points/photos/000/001/041/thumb_crop/data.jpg?1439230042)![pin](https://geotourist.com/img/point-pin.b715ed0f.svg)3

[Saguaro Forms and Cactus Flowers\\
\\
In 1973 the Wrigley family decided to sell the resort. The Talley family purchased it with the intention of turning into a year round resort destination. In order to do that, the family had to bring the resort up to current fire codes, which included the installation of a sprinkler system. As they were installing the pipes in the roof on the 4th floor, a welder’s torch sparked a fire, and resulted in a fire. It completely destroyed the 4th floor, and flooded the floors underneath it. To meet the scheduled opening date, Ms. Talley hired all of the students from Taliesin West, The Frank Lloyd Wright School of Architecture in Scottsdale Arizona, as well has a huge construction crew to completely renovate the main building. The project included the re-installation of the gold leaf ceiling. It was a 24-hour operation that lasted 81 days. \\
\\
In celebration of this amazing feat, Mrs. Wright donated the stained glass piece as a gift for the grand “reopening”. Frank Lloyd Wright had created this piece originally as a colored pencil drawing for a series of covers for Liberty Magazine in 1927. The magazine declined the artwork since they found it to be too radical for the times and they were afraid of losing their readership. Mrs. Wright found the drawing and commissioned an artist from Mesa, Arizona to create the stained glass in 1973.](https://geotourist.com/tours/401/Arizona_Biltmore_History_Tour/point/1041/Saguaro_Forms_and_Cactus_Flowers)

![point](https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/geotourist-content/points/photos/000/001/042/thumb_crop/data.jpg?1439230194)![pin](https://geotourist.com/img/point-pin.b715ed0f.svg)4

[The Sprites\\
\\
Another piece of Frank Lloyd Wright artwork are the Sprites that watch over the grounds at the Biltmore. The Sprites were designed by Wright in 1914 for the Midway Gardens, the premier dining venue on Lake Michigan, in Chicago Illinois. He had an Italian artist, Alfonso Ianelli sculpt the forms. When the Midway Gardens closed due to financial hardship and were demolished, the Sprites disappeared. They did not resurface until a lady by the name of Helen Raab purchased a farmland near Chicago and discovered the Sprites buried. She contacted Taliesin, the Frank Lloyd Wright school, to help recover and restore the Sprites. Three of the damaged Sprites were recovered and restored. \\
\\
In 1980, Mrs. Wright built a garden at Taliesin West and had them shipped for placement. Restoration and recasting was done on the originals. You may view 2 of the originals at Taliesin West in Scottsdale. In October of 1985, Taliesin donated the re-cast Sprites seen here, which watch over and adorn the Arizona Biltmore Resort. \\
\\
The Sprites were re-cast from the Solemn Sprite, which was used to reflect over the Chicago Midway summer gardens.](https://geotourist.com/tours/401/Arizona_Biltmore_History_Tour/point/1042/The_Sprites)

Show More
