markdown:
##### Entries on This Tour

[Start](https://theclio.com/tour/99/1)

[![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_5612_28032.63857.jpg)\\
\\
1\. Old Main, Marshall University \\
\\
Now the central administration building for Marshall University, Old Main dates back to 1838 with the construction of a small, four-room brick building to house Marshall Academy. The original structure was expanded with the addition of new sections in 1856, 1870, and 1896. The 1838 and 1856 portions were demolished in 1898 to allow for the construction of a much larger building that reflected Marshall and Huntington's growth. The final, major addition to Old Main was the distinct, Gothic section built on the western side in 1907. Old Main originally housed various facilities for Marshall including dormitories, classrooms, a library, auditorium, dining hall, and chapel. Today it is home to administrative offices and spaces for certain organizations. Old Main was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/1) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594064862812_cts.jpg)\\
\\
2\. Memories of Old Main\\
\\
Carter Taylor Seaton recounts attending classes and shopping at the school bookstore in Old Main.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/2) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_23247.49655.jpg)\\
\\
3\. John Deaver Drinko Library, Marshall University\\
\\
The John Deaver Drinko Library has been the primary library on campus since it opened in 1998. It stands at the former site of the College of Science Building, Northcott Hall (1915-1995), which was demolished to make room for the new library. Campus officials developed plans for a new library throughout the 1990s as a way to both replace the older Morrow Library and provide new technological and multimedia opportunities to students. The Drinko Library success in being built was that of both James Wade Gilley (President of Marshall University during 1991-1999) and John Deaver Drinko. In fact, the library was named in honor of prominent attorney John Deaver Drinko (a former student at Marshall University), for being one of the largest donor for the library project. Drinko gives Marshall students a place to study, collaborate with peers, utilize computers and access thousands of books, journals, and electronic materials. The library today contains over 180,000 books and other materials, reading and study areas, high-speed Internet and computers, presentation rooms, IT services such as that included but not limited to: houses offices of Information Technology, University Libraries, Instructional Technology, University Computing Services, and Telecommunications, a cafe, and a 24/7 computer lab.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/3) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_2691.227720.jpg)\\
\\
4\. Statue of John Marshall at Marshall University\\
\\
This eight-foot statue of John Marshall outside of the John Deaver Drinko Library was dedicated in 1998. The monument features a six-foot base engraved with the words "Revolutionary Soldier," "Definer of the Constitution," and "Devoted Husband and Father." John Marshall served in the Revolutionary War, explored and surveyed western Virginia, and shaped the federal judiciary while serving as the fourth Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court. Marshall was appointed Chief Justice on January 27, 1801, and he served until his death in 1835. Most historians agree that John Marshall was one of the most influential leaders of the early republic. More than any other individual in American history, John Marshall shaped the interpretation of the Constitution and established the Judicial Branch as an independent and equal branch of government.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/4) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594064910760_missymor.jpg)\\
\\
5\. Love of Marshall\\
\\
Missy Morrison discusses the impact that her Marshall education has had on her life.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/5) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_2156_20160503.08A.06-min.jpg)\\
\\
6\. Marshall University Memorial Fountain \\
\\
Designed by artist Harry Bertoia and dedicated in 1972, this fountain pays tribute to the seventy-five people who perished in the 1970 Marshall University Plane Crash and the resilience of the university community. Built of welded copper and bronze tubes, the fountain represents life and upward growth and stands in the middle of the Memorial Student Center plaza. From the time of its dedication, this monument has become the central landmark on campus and is the site of an annual ceremony held here each year on November 14, the anniversary of the crash. During the ceremony, the fountain is turned off in remembrance of the 75 who perished that day. The two audio files embedded within this entry include portions of speeches given at the dedication of the fountain and reflections from members of the Marshall University community.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/6) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_3395_Corbly%20Hall1654.jpg)\\
\\
7\. Corbly Hall, Marshall University\\
\\
Corbly Hall is the home of Marshall University's internationally accredited Lewis College of Business as well as the English and Economics Departments. When the four story building was dedicated in November 1980, it was the largest academic building in the West Virginia state system of higher education. It includes some of the largest lecture halls on campus, one of which holds up to 150 people. The facility is named after Lawrence J. Corbly (1862-1935) who served as the last principal and first president of Marshall College from 1896 until 1915. Corbly made significant improvements to Marshall during his tenure, including growing the student body and increasing the quality of the school's curriculum.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/7) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_8453_1.jpg)\\
\\
8\. Brad D. Smith Foundation Hall and Erickson Alumni Center, Marshall University\\
\\
The Erickson Alumni Center serves as the headquarters of the Marshall University Foundation. The Foundation is a non-profit, alumni organization established in 1947 and works to provide financial support for Marshall University. The Center is named after businessman Charlie O. Erickson, who funded the creation of alumni centers at numerous colleges across West Virginia. In 2010 the Center moved into the newly-constructed Brad D. Smith Foundation Hall. It is named after prominent businessman, Marshall graduate, and donor Brad D. Smith, who has contributed millions of dollars to various projects at Marshall. The foundation hall houses offices and alumni facilities, as well as space for lectures, receptions, and private events.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/8) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594064960751_holmes.jpg)\\
\\
9\. Growth of the Alumni Association\\
\\
Linda Holmes briefly recounts the evolution of Marshall's Alumni Association.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/9) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_5605_Memorial%20Student%20Center1731.jpg)\\
\\
10\. Memorial Student Center, Marshall University \\
\\
The Marshall University Memorial Student Center opened in 1971 to provide students with a place to socialize, rest, and study on campus. It replaced an older facility, the Shawkey Student Union, that had been in use since 1933. The MSC was named in honor of the victims of the November 14, 1970 plane crash and serves as a living memorial. Today it houses a food court, lounge areas, the campus bookstore, a recreational area, various offices, and several meeting rooms, dining halls, and event spaces.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/10) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594065010870_We-are-marshall-lores.jpg)\\
\\
11\. Filming "We Are Marshall"\\
\\
Mike Kirtner discusses the filming of the iconic boardroom scene from the movie "We Are Marshall."](https://theclio.com/tour/99/11) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_23776.51367.jpg)\\
\\
12\. Joan C. Edwards Performing Arts Center\\
\\
The Joan C. Edwards Performing Arts Center is home of the Marshall University MU School of Theatre, featuring two venues, the Joan C. Edwards Playhouse stage and the smaller, Francis-Booth Experimental Theatre. Adjacent is the Jomie Jazz Center. Along with performance space and a spacious lobby and atrium, the center has classrooms, space for stage design, workshops, and more. Marshall University Theatre shares the box office in the Joan C. Edwards Performing Arts Center with the Marshall Artists Series.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/12) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_6213_Schoolhouse%201.jpg)\\
\\
13\. One-Room School Museum, Marshall University\\
\\
This historic one-room schoolhouse, which houses the Ovie and Jesse Cline Museum, preserves the legacy of rural education in Appalachia. The building dates back to 1888, when it served as a schoolhouse for a rural part of Cabell County. It remained open until 1955, at a time when one-room schoolhouses across the county were closed in favor of larger, consolidated school systems. After being used as a storage shed for many years, the schoolhouse was relocated to the campus of Marshall University in 1995 thanks to the efforts of Paul Lutz, a History Department faculty member. The museum was named after the parents of Phil Cline, who attended and taught in one-room schools. The interior presents a recreation of a one-room schoolhouse, with Peabody-style desks, era-appropriate books, and a pot belly stove. The museum is open by appointment.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/13) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594065070457_kirtner.jpg)\\
\\
14\. Marshall in the '60s.\\
\\
Mike Kirtner recalls a peaceful student protest against the Vietnam War on the front lawn of Old Main.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/14) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_39741.98649.jpg)\\
\\
15\. Education Building, Marshall University\\
\\
This building was constructed in 1937 and known as Jenkins Hall until 2020. The building originally served as a laboratory school where enrollees of the college's teacher preparation program could teach students under the guidance of experienced teachers and their professors. The school served grades kindergarten through twelve until 1970 when the building was repurposed to house Marshall University classes and offices. The third-oldest building on campus, the Education Building includes the Learning Resource Center, a mathematics education laboratory, a science education laboratory, an electronic classroom, and the June Harless Center for Rural Educational Research and Development. The building was originally named for Confederate General and Cabell County native Albert Gallatin Jenkins, a controversial figure in his own time following a raid in Pennsylvania where his men captured and sold Black women and children into slavery. In 2020, the Board of Governors reversed a previous decision and voted unanimously to remove Jenkins' name in the wake of protests around the nation that were a response to the police killing of Goerge Floyd.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/15) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1566_Gullickson%20Hall1501.jpg)\\
\\
16\. Gullickson Hall, Marshall University \\
\\
Gullickson Hall was built in 1961 to accommodate a growing student population. It originally housed physical education classrooms, facilities for sports teams to practice, and space for intramural and recreational activities. Originally called the Men's Health and Physical Education Building, the structure was renamed in 1964 after former physical education professor Otto A. "Swede" Gullickson. Gullickson worked at Marshall for over 30 years, overseeing the development of the school's intramural program into one of the largest in the nation.Today Gullickson Hall is attached to the adjacent Cam Henderson Center, and it is home to the Marshall ROTC program.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/16) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594065145817_hayes.jpg)\\
\\
17\. My Dad, the President\\
\\
Mark Hayes talks about attending Marshall while his father, Bob Hayes, was the university president.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/17) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_5935_29786.68562.jpg)\\
\\
18\. Harris Hall, Marshall University\\
\\
Harris Hall was dedicated in 1976 and is named in honor of Arvil Ernest Harris, who was a political science and social studies professor, as well as the first Dean of the Graduate School. Harris Hall replaced Music Hall, a former retail space purchased by Marshall in 1926 and used to house the Music Department until the construction of Smith Music Hall. Throughout its history Harris Hall has housed many of Marshall's liberal arts programs. Today it is home to the history, geography, psychology, counseling, classics, philosophy, and religious studies departments.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/18) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1387_Science%20Building%20Add-On.jpg)\\
\\
19\. Science Building, Marshall University\\
\\
Marshall University's Science Building was constructed in 1950 to replace Northcott Science Hall. Due to a growing enrollment rate, the Science Building expanded in 1984 to offer better laboratories and lecture halls. The Science Building is home to the College of Science, the Schools of Biological and Environmental Sciences, Forensic & Criminal Justice Sciences, Mathematics & Applied Information, and Physical Sciences.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/19) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594065281493_mumed.jpg)\\
\\
20\. The School of Medicine's Humble Beginnings\\
\\
Linda Holmes describes the origins of the Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/20) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_19265.42619.jpg)\\
\\
21\. Arthur Weisberg Family Applied Engineering Complex\\
\\
The Arthur Weisburg Family Applied Engineering Complex was opened in August of 2015, and offers engineering students state of the art equipment. Marshall University did not have an engineering building on campus for nearly thirty years until the installation of the Arthur Weisburg Family Engineering Laboratories building in 2006. The West Virginia Board of Regents phased out the engineering program at Marshall University in the early 1970s, and did not revive the program until the early 2000s. Art Weisburg is the owner of State Electric, and donated generously so that Marshall could once again host an engineering program.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/21) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594065369570_stevew.jpg)\\
\\
22\. Commencement Recollections\\
\\
Steve Williams describes his two graduation ceremonies and how the keynote speakers have influenced his career.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/22) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1479_1.jpg)\\
\\
23\. James E. Morrow Library and Marshall Special Collections\\
\\
Morrow Library was named after former University President, James E. Morrow, and was completed in 1931 to replace the original library on the second floor of Old Main. When the library first opened, it housed study areas and Marshall’s art school. In 1965, a project began to expand the library and added the stacks towers along with wraparound additions to the side and back of the building. During this renovation, the main study hall was split into two floors, and was completed in 1967. In 1998, the John Deaver Drinko Library opened and became Marshall’s main library. However, Morrow continued to serve Marshall by housing the University Special Collections. Today the library is home to a variety of collections and the university’s more rare and valuable books. Some of Morrow’s major collections are the Rosanna Blake Civil War Collection, the Hoffman Medical Science collection, and the Chuck Yeager Collection.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/23) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1062_smith-hall.jpg)\\
\\
24\. Smith Hall, Marshall University\\
\\
Smith Hall is an academic complex that consists of Stewart Smith Hall, Evelyn Hollberg Smith Music Hall, the Birke Art Gallery, and the Communications Building. The building opened in 1967 and replaced a former naval barracks that acted as temporary classrooms. Smith Hall is named after popular longtime Marshall President Stewart H. Smith, who served from 1946 to 1968. Today the facility is utilized for many general education classes. It is home to many College of Liberal Arts and College of Arts and Media Departments, including the W. Page Pitt School of Journalism and Mass Communications and the School of Music. Smith Hall also contains a student lounge, cafe, speech clinic, offices for The Parthenon, and the WMUL radio station.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/24) [![](https://storage.googleapis.com/clio-images/small_1594065206794_BradSmith_square.jpg)\\
\\
25\. Marshall University's Character\\
\\

26\. Marshall University Bench Honoring Freedom Rider Joan Browning \\
\\
Dedicated June 8, 2025, this bench recognizes Joan Browning, a West Virginian who was one of 436 Freedom Riders who participated in protests against segregation in 1961. Browning was a student and instructor at Marshall University and received an honorary doctorate from the University in 2024. In addition to a long career in support of the civil rights movement, Browning was the last person selected to join what would become the final Freedom Ride. She was jailed in Albany, Georgia, and chose to remain in solitary confinement rather than accept bail. After the Freedom Rides, Joan Browning moved to Atlanta and later served as a secretary for the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC). In this role, she worked closely with leaders like Julian Bond and Ella Baker.](https://theclio.com/tour/99/26)

## What to Expect

The largest section of Acadia National Park is located on Mount Desert Island. It’s a national park unlike most others as much of the park is designated as chunks of land around the island – from one end to the other. This makes touring Acadia National Park an even more enjoyable experience because it creates an interesting mix of natural features, great hikes, superb sightseeing and rugged coastline that you would expect from a park. But there is the bonus of many fascinating places, working harbor towns, historical sites, manicured gardens and great little towns and surprises.

Since our travels will take us all over Mount Desert Island, we’ve created the tour with two separate loop routes.  Both start and finish near Bar Harbor. Our advice is to spend one day on each loop if you have the time. If you are trying to do the whole island in one day, do the Park Loop Road first, and then finish your day on the Mount Desert Island Loop. And try to get started early!

### Suggested Start Location

Thompson Island Visitor Center, Hulls Cove Visitor Center or Bar Harbor.

### How Much Time Do I Need?

At least two full days is recommended.

### Driving Distance

Approx. 90 miles.

## FAQ

#### WHAT IS SO SPECIAL ABOUT ACADIA NATIONAL PARK?

[Acadia National Park is New England’s only national park](https://guidealong.com/acadia-national-park/), and ranks high on many travel bucket lists. With rugged granite cliffs along the coast, miles of forested trails and its incredible fall foilage, it’s perfect for sightseeing and outdoor adventures.

#### WHAT IS THE BEST TIME TO VISIT ACADIA NATIONAL PARK?

Although Acadia National Park is open year round, [the best time to visit is from late May through October](https://guidealong.com/acadia-national-park/#when). The Island Explorer shuttle bus operates from late June to mid October, and that’s when everything is open.

Spring means being prepared for everything from wet cold and perhaps snow to warm sunny days. Some hiking trails close for nesting birds; other park facilities may be closed for maintenance. Autumn in Acadia brings cooler and dryer weather and changing foliage.

#### HOW MANY DAYS DO YOU NEED FOR ACADIA NATIONAL PARK?

While you can drive the Park Loop Road and loop around to the western side of the island in a day, [you’ll want at least 2-5 days to fully explore Acadia National Park](https://guidealong.com/acadia-national-park/#time), hike, bike, enjoy other island attractions, and perhaps ferry or drive to the Schoodic section.

#### CAN YOU DRIVE THROUGH ACADIA NATIONAL PARK?

One of the park’s main attractions, the [27-mile Park Loop Road](https://guidealong.com/acadia-national-park-trip-planner/#highlights) is the go-to scenic drive around the east side of Mount Desert Island, and connects Acadia’s lakes, mountains, and shoreline.

## Trip Planning

### Note for International Visitors

This park has additional fees for international visitors as of 2026. Visit the [NPS](https://www.nps.gov/planyourvisit/passes.htm) website for details.

## About The Tour

Wander cobblestone streets, admire Federal-style row houses, and uncover the layered history of Boston’s most charming neighborhood!

Here are just a few of the fun things you can do on the tour!

• Snap a photo on Boston’s most photographed and charming cobblestone lane.

• Walk past elegant townhouses in one of Boston’s most exclusive squares.

• Admire the golden dome of this historic seat of government.

• Grab a drink or photo at the bar that inspired Cheers.

• Visit the duck statues in the park inspired by the beloved book.

## 3\. What should I budget for the Beacon Hill Tour?  ![Down](https://www.shakaguide.com/shakaguide/img/tour/dropdown-icon-new.png)

- **Souvenirs and shopping**: $10–$50, depending on the item﻿


## 4\. What are the park hours for the Beacon Hill Tour?  ![Down](https://www.shakaguide.com/shakaguide/img/tour/dropdown-icon-new.png)

- ﻿Robert Gould Shaw and 54th Regiment Memorial: Boston Common open 6 am-11:30 pm
- Massachusetts State House:


  - Tours are given weekdays, 10 am-3:30 pm daily.

  - The building is open for self-guided tours weekdays 8:45 am-5 pm.

  - Closed on weekends and holidays.


- Otis House Museum: Tours June-Oct Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays 11 am-4 pm

- Museum of African American History: 10 am-4 pm Tues-Sun

- Nichols House Museum:


  - Tours offered Tues-Sat: 10 am, 11 am, and 12 pm.

  - Sun: 11 am, 12 pm, 1 pm.


- Cheers:


  - 11 am-9 pm Sun-Wed

  - 11 am -1 pm Thurs-Sat


- Make Way for Ducklings Sculpture: Boston Public Garden open 6 am-11:30 pm

- Good Will Hunting Bench: Boston Public Garden open 6 am-11:30 pm﻿

# Your Guide. Your Time. Your Way.

## Unlock the Road in 3 Steps

Epic Trips. Made Simple

### Choose your tour

Browse 230+ walking and driving tours packed with stories, landmarks, and history

### Access Your Tour

Download the Action Tour Guide app and sign in with the same email address used for your website purchase. For partner bookings, enter the password provided. Your tour will appear under My Tours.

### Download your tour

Download your tour before you go. Once downloaded, no internet or cell signal is needed.

## 3 Easy Steps

To the best road trip ever.

### Choose your tour

Browse 200+ walking and driving tours packed with stories, landmarks, and history

### Access your tour

Download the Action Tour Guide app and sign in with the same email address used for your website purchase. For partner bookings, enter the password provided. Your tour will appear under My Tours.

### Download your tour

![ATG App 768x432 1 scaled 1](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

![how it works thumbnail](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## An audio guide, map, and a tour book

Our GPS-enabled app makes exploring easy and fun! Each of our 200+ tours includes a GPS-guided route and lively audio commentary that plays automatically as you reach each location. Simply follow the route to uncover must-see sights, fascinating history, and hidden gems.

## Freedom To Explore

Ditch the crowded buses and rigid schedules, you’re free to explore on your terms. Whether you’re solo, with family, kids, or pets, you can pause, snap photos, and soak in the sights as long as you like. This is your journey, your way.

![Freedom To Explore](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

![Works Offline](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## Works Offline

Download tours in advance and explore seamlessly, even without service. Navigate and enjoy storytelling anywhere.

## Experience the Stories

Why did the brave stand their ground at Gettysburg? What secrets do the terrains of Yellowstone hold? With us, you don’t just visit – you experience, understand, and connect.

![Experience The Stories](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

![Tour Any Time Any Day](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## Tour Anytime, Any Day

Your purchase never expires. Download your tour today and enjoy it whenever you’re ready.

Endorsed by [Thrillist](https://actiontourguide.com/achievements/) and [WBZ](https://actiontourguide.com/achievements/), our app’s credibility is top-notch. Winning the Laurel Award from Newport Mansions highlights our storytelling passion.

### From tourist to explorer   in just one click

Explore at your own pace and safely with a personal guide on your phone. There’s no need for a crowded tour group.

Get a private guide in your pocket filled with current, high-quality, and locally sourced content that’s as good as a friend’s recommendation for taking you off the beaten paths.

### It’s hands-free and immersive.  Shh, just listen.

What’s that majestic structure in front of you? Plug in your headphones and find out.

SmartGuide sends expertly crafted, engaging audio-stories straight to your ears, so you can stay fully immersed in the world around you, wherever you go.

## The app that turns your smartphone into an audio tour guide to   Long Beach, California

Just Ahead frees you from fumbling for maps or flipping through guidebooks. You simply drive as we guide you to all of the city’s many wonders.

[Download on theApp Store](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/just-ahead-gps-audio-guides/id814596586?mt=8) [Download forAndroid](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.justahead.justaheadandroid)

Written by National Geographic and Outside Magazine author Bob Howells

Covers all the highlights of one of Southern California's great beach cities

Where to play, walk, shop, dine, tour, and experience history

**The Urban Waterfront Playground**

Just Ahead’s GPS-guided audio tour of Long Beach, California, is a narrated guide to Southern California’s urban waterfront playground. Our tour takes you to and through a city that makes the most of its remarkable location, stretched along more than five miles of gorgeous California beaches. As with all of our audio guides, once you download it from the Apple App Store or Google Play, you don’t need an Internet connection or mobile-phone signal to use it. Just turn it on, drive, and enjoy. We narrate what you’re seeing, in real time.

**Sample a few of the 200+ stories that play automatically as you drive through Long Beach:**

![](https://www.justahead.com/wp-includes/images/media/audio.svg)

We show you all the top attractions of Long Beach, its hidden gems, and its distinctive neighborhoods. Kids love Long Beach, as we suggest the best places for families to explore and to play. We also show you the city’s cultural core and its hip, vibrant districts. We suggest urban walks, nature walks, and even guide you along the city’s Shoreline bike and pedestrian path.

As you approach each sight, we tell you all about it. Highlights include:

**Queen Mary • Aquarium of the Pacific • The Canals of Naples • Downtown’s Restaurant Row • East Village Arts District • Shoreline Village • Retro Row • Alamitos Bay Beach • Shoreline Pedestrian Bike Path • Rainbow Harbor • Belmont Pier • Shoreline Marina • Alamitos Bay Marina • Rancho Los Alamitos • Rancho Los Cerritos • Bixby Knolls • Museum of Latin American Art • Long Beach Museum of Art • Battleship USS Iowa • Bluff Park • Alamitos Peninsula • Catalina Island**

As a waterfront playground, Long Beach is all about being active, and we steer you toward all the best places for:

**Swimming • Bicycling • Jogging • Sailing • Kayaking • Stand-up Paddleboarding • Boating • Kiteboarding • Yoga • Dog Walking • Beach Volleyball • Walking • Gondola Ride**

Just Ahead’s tour of Long Beach is more than selection of highlights. We also tell you about its fascinating history, architecture, and arts in a series of in-depth bonus stories that include

**Art Deco Walking Tour • How the Queen Mary Came to Long Beach • Day Tripping to Catalina • Toyota Grand Prix of Long Beach • The “Oil Islands” • The World’s Longest Breakwater • Two-Minute History of Long Beach • Art Deco Heritage**

With Just Ahead, you get a full, rich, engaging, and entertaining experience of one of the most entertaining cities on the West Coast. It’s like having a friendly tour guide along for the ride!

## Works Offline

Tours & Maps Included

## Tour Highlights

- Cathedral of Saint Raphael

A majestic downtown landmark and the tour's starting point, free to step inside if it's open.

- Hotel Julien Dubuque

A historic hotel dating back nearly 150 years, still standing as a cornerstone of downtown Dubuque's story.

- Fenelon Place Elevator

The world's shortest, steepest scenic railway, a two-minute ride for four dollars with views stretching across three states on a clear day.

- Washington Park

A green downtown gathering space where Dubuquers have relaxed, played, and celebrated for generations.

- Dubuque Museum of Art

Home to works by Grant Wood, famous for "American Gothic," with admission at seven dollars for adults.

- Dubuque Town Clock

A downtown landmark marking the heart of the historic district.

- The Grand Opera House

A storied performance venue reflecting Dubuque's rich cultural history.

- Dubuque County Courthouse

A grand architectural landmark and the tour's closing stop.

### Frequently Asked Questions

- How long does the Dubuque walking tour take?

Most visitors complete the full route in about one and a half to two hours, longer if you stop inside the museum or ride the Fenelon Place Elevator.

- Does this tour work offline?

Yes. Download the tour before you go and it works completely offline, with no data connection required.

- Are there admission fees along the tour?

Most stops are free, though the Fenelon Place Elevator costs four dollars for adults and the Dubuque Museum of Art is seven dollars for adults.

- Is this tour good for kids?

Yes. The Fenelon Place Elevator ride and Washington Park are especially popular with families.

- How much walking is involved?

The route covers a little over a mile through downtown Dubuque, including a gentle climb near the Cathedral Historic District.

- What is the Fenelon Place Elevator?

The tour explains how this landmark became known as the world's shortest, steepest scenic railway, built to carry a former mayor down the bluff to work and back.

- Where does the tour start and end?

It starts at the Cathedral of Saint Raphael and ends at the Dubuque County Courthouse.

- Can I pause the tour to explore the museum or ride the elevator?

Yes. The tour is designed to pause naturally at each stop so you can go inside the museum, ride the elevator, or explore Washington Park before continuing.

- Who is Grant Wood, and why does he matter to Dubuque?

The tour explains the connection between the Dubuque Museum of Art's collection and Grant Wood, the Iowa artist famous for painting "American Gothic."

- What is Dubuque best known for?

Dubuque is known for its riverboat history along the Mississippi, its well-preserved 19th-century architecture, and landmarks like the Fenelon Place Elevator.

# Audio Guide: Toronto Downtwon Walking Tour (Self Guided), Toronto

Sprawling on the northwestern shore of Lake Ontario, the capital of the Canadian province of Ontario, Toronto, is a major metropolis renowned for its dynamic pace and high-rising skyline, incorporating both ultra-modern skyscrapers and historic architecture.

The area of present-day Toronto has been inhabited for thousands of years. Its first known settlers – the Wyandot (or Huron) people – had occupied the region long before the 1500s, followed later by the Iroquois tribe. The name Toronto is likely derived from the Iroquoian word “tkaronto”, which means the place where trees stand in water. Another theory suggests that Toronto means "plenty" and was adopted by the French in the 1630s as part of their lexicon originating from the Huron and Iroquoian languages.

Following the so-called Toronto Purchase of 1787, the British took over the territory and established here a town called York. In 1834, the town was incorporated as a city and subsequently renamed Toronto. Thirty-three years later, the city became the capital of the Ontario province within the Canadian Confederation.

Around the same time, a thriving industrial area developed around Toronto Harbour and the lower Don River mouth, linked by rail and water to the rest of Canada and the United States. Traces of that period include the Gooderham Distillery, once the world's largest whisky manufacturer, which is now part of the historic "Distillery District".

Waves of immigration in the 19th and 20th centuries saw the arrival in Toronto of European settlers (Irish, German, French, Italian, Russian, Polish, and Jewish), as well as Chinese. Such ethnic diversity is presently reflected in local neighborhoods, such as Chinatown, Kensington Market, and others.

The post-WWII boom resulted in a rapid expansion of Toronto, largely contributing to its cultural and urban development, resulting in a wealth of entertainment and recreational facilities. Shopping areas like St. Lawrence Market and Toronto Eaton Centre are recognized as the city's most popular attractions, drawing annually millions of visitors.

Torontonians take their sport seriously, especially when it comes to their much-loved ice hockey. No visit to the city is complete without getting a glimpse of this fascinating game – best done at the Hockey Hall of Fame!

Traveling on foot is advantageous in Toronto, as it comes to life with its blend of quirky sights, sounds, and unique architecture. For a more detailed acquaintance with the historical and modern capital of Ontario and a chance to explore some of its prominent landmarks, embark on this self-guided introductory walk.

[Image Courtesy of Flickr and The City of Toronto.](https://www.flickr.com/photos/cityoftoronto/4557762400/)

**How it works:** Download the app "GPSmyCity: Walks in 1K+ Cities" from [Apple App Store](https://www.gpsmycity.com/dlnk/?view=guide&id=211&src=2) or [Google Play Store](https://www.gpsmycity.com/dlnk/?view=guide&id=211&src=3) to your mobile phone or tablet. The app turns your mobile device into a personal tour guide and its built-in GPS navigation functions guide you from one tour stop to next. The app works offline, so no data plan is needed when traveling abroad.

iPhone, iPad

Ready for one more road trip? Summer’s winding down, but there’s still time to hit the road. From Maui to Yellowstone download the app and find your next adventure.

Meet your personal tour guide in an app! Shaka Guide has 90+ audio tours across the country in places like Hawaii, Yellowstone National Park, Grand Teton, Yosemite, Sedona, Gettysburg, Salem, the Boston Freedom Trail, Utah's Mighty 5 and more.

HOW A GPS AUDIO TOUR WORKS
The app uses GPS to play audio narration automatically as you drive or walk. Shaka Guide’s audio tours provide directions to must-see stops, stories about the places you’re visiting, travel tips, and local music. It's like having a personal tour guide along for the ride!

TOUR ON YOUR TERMS
Upgrade your road trip on a GPS audio tour! With Shaka Guide, you’ll get the insights of a tour guide with the freedom to explore on your terms. Shaka Guide has planned the itinerary, picked the must-see stops, and has hours of stories to share. But, with Shaka Guide what you see and do is up to you – pick the stops you want and skip the ones you don’t.

AUDIO TOUR GUIDE + OFFLINE MAP
So, what exactly is a GPS audio tour? Imagine you combined a travel guide, sightseeing app, and audio guide all in one - that’s a GPS audio tour! The app uses GPS to give you directions to popular sites with stories, music and travel tips (like bathroom and food stops) as you guide along on your travels. And, with a reliable offline map, the app still works when there’s no service.

NEW YELLOWSTONE TOUR GUIDE
Check out the NEW Yellowstone GPS audio Tour. Spend 1-7 days in Yellowstone National Park with your very own personal guide. The Yellowstone Tour has starting points at all of the park's entrances - just pick a section of the park, turn the app on, and explore. The Yellowstone Tour also works in multiple directions! The timing is perfect with detailed history lessons as you travel through Yellowstone National Park. Don't visit Yellowstone National Park without Shaka Guide's Yellowstone National Park GPS audio Tour!

HAWAII AUDIO TOUR GUIDE
Shaka Guide has the #1-rated travel apps for Maui, Oahu, Kauai, and Big Island. Stay just ahead of your Hawaii trip planning and visit spots like the Road to Hana on Maui, Oahu's Grand Circle Island, Volcanoes National Park on the Big Island, or Waimea Canyon in Kauai with a Shaka Guide GPS audio tour by your side!

MAUI AUDIO TOUR GUIDE
Shaka Guide is the highest-rated tour app in Maui and the Road to Hana. Explore Maui with 6 GPS audio Tours including Maui's most beloved road trip - the Classic Road to Hana. Other Maui Tours include Reverse Road to Hana, Loop Road to Hana, West Maui Coastline, and Sunrise and Sunset at Haleakala.

NATIONAL PARK AUDIO TOUR GUIDE
Visit America's top national parks with a GPS tour guide! Guide along on tours including Yellowstone National Park, Yosemite, Grand Teton, Hawaii Volcanoes, Shenandoah, Utah's Mighty 5, and more!

Bundle + Save - Get the Yellowstone National Park + Grand Teton Audio Tour Bundle for $23.99

AMERICA'S FAVORITE ROAD TRIPS - AUDIO TOUR GUIDE
The ultimate audio tour guide for scenic drives like the Road to Hana in Maui, Sedona, Lake Tahoe, and more! Also, check out day trips in Tuscon and Las Vegas. You'll seamlessly guide along these scenic road trips without missing any of the action. A tour guide by your side – it's that simple.

It’s very informative, has great stops for sightseeing and tasty food, and the GPS worked very well even in areas with little service. HOWEVER, and this is a huge however, TURN AROUND when they suggest you turn around. iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch

300+ GPS Self Guided Tours

WalknTours transforms your phone into a personal tour guide, delivering GPS-triggered audio stories that automatically play as you walk or drive. Explore Cities, National Parks & Scenic Drives on curated planned tours, anytime, at your own pace.

Explore over 300 self-guided tours across 260+ destinations, including historic downtowns, famous landmarks, haunted locations, scenic drives, and national parks.

Features

• 300+ guided tours across 270+ destinations
• GPS-guided audio narration that plays automatically
• Walking tours and driving tours
• Offline access after download
• Explore at your own pace

Haunted & Ghost Tours

Love the paranormal?

WalknTours features one of the largest collections of self-guided ghost tours, allowing you to explore haunted locations, local legends, mysterious events, and chilling stories across the United States and beyond.

Included is a built-in EMF Ghost Detector that lets paranormal enthusiasts add an extra layer of fun while exploring haunted sites.

New AI Walking Tour Creator

Create your own AI-powered walking tour anywhere in the world.

Our AI Tour Creator generates personalized walking tours complete with routes, points of interest, narration, and local stories. Simply choose a location and start exploring.

Available in 10 languages for travelers worldwide.

New Driving Tours

Discover the road less traveled with our growing collection of driving tours.

Explore:
• National Parks
• Scenic Drives
• Coastal Routes
• Historic Roads
• Small-Town Adventures

Now available in 50+ destinations and growing.

Perfect For

• Travelers and tourists
• History lovers
• Ghost hunters and paranormal enthusiasts
• Road trippers
• Families
• Solo explorers
• Weekend adventurers

Download WalknTours and start exploring today.

How to take a tour?
Go to the tours start, press play, and WalknTours guides you step by step through the streets telling you its story. It's like an in person tour guide, only it's on your phone, way more convenient, more entertaining and a better story teller.

To see a list of cities download the app and choose 'preview tours' to see if we have a tour near you. Or visit walkntours.com to see a list of cities.

Tours can be purchased individually in the WalknTours app or as an annual subscription. Annual subscriptions unlock all the tours in the WalknTours app for a period of one year.
WalknTours Subscription
• Subscription is charged annually. You will be granted an annual auto-renewable subscription.
• The payment will be charged to your iTunes Account.
• A subscription automatically renews unless auto-renew is turned off at least 24-hours before the end of the current period.
• Your account will be charged for renewal within 24-hours prior to the end of the current period.
• To manage auto-renewal please visit your iTunes Account Settings after purchase.
• If you cancel the subscription, the tours in the WalknTours app will be locked and you will only be able to see their descriptions and hear the tour introduction.
• For terms of use please refer to the standard Apple Terms of Use (EULA)
• WalknTours Standard Privacy Policy and Terms of Use https://www.walkntours.com/privacypolicy

iPhone, iPad

The Travel App That Turns Your Smartphone Into a GPS Audio Tour Guide for Your Vacation Road Trips

Just Ahead is the perfect road trip app. With its guided tours and offline maps, you feel like you have a friendly tour guide along—and you don’t need an Internet connection or mobile phone signal to enjoy the narrated audio tour.

••• ‘BEST TRAVEL APP’—North America Travel Journalists Assoc. •••
••• ‘BEST APP’—Sunset Magazine •••
••• TOP FIVE NEW TRAVEL APPS—USA TODAY •••

• ROAD TRIPS BROUGHT TO LIFE! •
Just Ahead’s travel guides tell you what you’re seeing as you drive through America’s most compelling destinations.

GPS prompts the app to deliver spoken descriptions and stories of the scenery and sights just outside your car window.

No more thumbing through guidebooks or fumbling for maps. You see a sight and wonder, “What’s that?” Just then, Just Ahead tells you what you’re seeing!

••• WHY IT’S THE BEST TRAVEL APP •••

• Works Offline •
Audio guides and built-in maps don’t need an Internet connection or a mobile phone signal.

• More Points of Interest •
Just Ahead tour guides contain more points of interest and stories than any other audio travel guides.

• Inside Information •
Each guide is written by an expert author and spoken by a professional narrator. You simply drive, while Just Ahead informs and entertains you.

• Great Stories •
The scenery comes alive: notes on wildlife, geology, flora, history, people.

• Easy to Use •
Just Ahead audio tour guides play automatically. Just turn on the app and begin driving—it talks whenever there’s something informative or entertaining to say!

• Helpful Suggested Directions •
Just Ahead guides you to and from your destination. It tells you why you should turn or not, what you should do after a turn, and recommends the best direction to take.

• Family Friendly •
Just Ahead audio guides create shared experiences, conversations, and memories that will last a lifetime.

• FREE TRIAL! •
Audio tour guides are available as in-app purchases and range from FREE–$19.99. Each guide includes a full-function free trial and free updates.

••• AVAILABLE GUIDES •••

Explore GPS-guided audio tours for historic sites, scenic drives, cities, national parks, and more.. Hear the stories, use offline maps, and travel on your schedule.

Go beyond the must-see sights with Action Tour Guide. Discover the fascinating stories behind iconic landmarks and hidden gems with 230+ self-guided audio tours across 40+ U.S. states and 15+ countries. Explore on your schedule as expert narration turns the sights you see into stories you’ll remember. Clear directions and offline maps to keep you on track - even without cell service. No tour bus, no timetable, no expiry. Your trip, taken further.

How It Works:
Turn your phone into a personal tour guide with Action Tour Guide. Start at the recommended location or join anywhere along the route, then follow the map as GPS automatically plays engaging stories, turn-by-turn directions, and helpful travel tips. No searching, scrolling, or tapping at every stop. Pause, explore, skip ahead, or continue whenever you’re ready - all at your own pace.

Why You’ll Love Action Tour Guide
‣ Explore Your Way: Start whenever you’re ready, pause to enjoy the moment, and continue later right where you left off.
‣ Stories Come to Life: Fascinating stories, directions, and helpful tips play automatically at just the right moment as you drive or walk.
‣ Works Offline: Download your tour before you go, then keep exploring wherever the road takes you - even in remote areas without internet or cell service.
‣ 230+ Driving and Walking Tours: Discover historic sites, scenic drives, cities, national parks and hidden gems worldwide.

The narrator does an excellent job narrating and gives you inside tips you don't get from any travel guide I've ever used. The App itself is easy to navigate and clicking on the More Information button at the bottom gives you specific instructions on the hike you my choose to embark on. Very helpful! You can click on the Map button and it shows you exactly where you are at. You just start the app once and it starts and stops as you move through the parks. I bought a Travel Book and hardly used it because Action Tours App was so complete. The background info provided also gives you a deeper appreciation for your surroundings. The graphics are beautiful and really help you to identify specific landmarks. The app gives you options to do the trails or hikes associated with each stop. # Audioguía Otumba: Choque de Culturas e Ingeniería Monumental

Te damos la más cordial bienvenida a **Otumba**, un rincón fundamental del Estado de México cuyo suelo ha sido testigo de los eventos más dramáticos y transformadores de nuestra historia nacional. Esta **Audioguía Otumba** ha sido diseñada de forma estratégica para llevarte a través de plazas tranquilas, templos virreinales y monumentos colosales, revelando cómo esta antigua provincia prehispánica se convirtió en un eje de comunicación e ingeniería sin precedentes en el Nuevo Mundo.

## Itinerario Maestro de la Audioguía Otumba

Para ofrecerte una experiencia cómoda, lógica y con un flujo ideal, el recorrido se ha organizado iniciando con un circuito peatonal por el centro histórico y concluyendo con sus impresionantes joyas arquitectónicas e industriales periféricas:

### Fase 1: Memoria de la Conquista y Tradición Local (Recorrido a Pie)

- **Plaza de la Constitución y Monumento a la Batalla de Otumba:** El punto donde el ejército de Hernán Cortés libró uno de los enfrentamientos más feroces contra los guerreros mexicas en 1520, cambiando el rumbo de la conquista.

- **Ex Convento de la Inmaculada Concepción:** Una joya franciscana del siglo XVI edificada sobre un antiguo basamento prehispánico, que destaca por la sobriedad de su arquitectura y su imponente atrio.

- **El Santuario del Burro (Burrolandia):** Una de las estaciones más singulares y entrañables de nuestra **Audioguía Otumba**, un espacio dedicado a la conservación, protección y celebración de este noble animal, profundamente ligado a la vida agrícola y cultural de la región.


### Fase 2: Ingeniería Civil y Patrimonio de la Humanidad (En Vehículo)

- **Antigua Estación de Ferrocarril:** Un vestigio industrial del siglo XIX que narra el auge comercial y la modernización del transporte en el centro del país.

- **Acueducto del Padre Tembleque:** El espectacular cierre de nuestra **Audioguía Otumba**. Una proeza monumental de la ingeniería hidráulica del siglo XVI, reconocida como Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO. Su arcada mayor desafía la geografía del valle y fusiona los conocimientos arquitectónicos europeos con la maestría de la mano de obra indígena, creando una pintura visual sobrecogedora en medio del paisaje semiárido.


## ¿Por qué elegir la Audioguía Otumba de Audioguías a la Mexicana?

Recorrer Otumba exige comprender la profundidad de los procesos sociales que unieron a dos mundos. Nuestra **Audioguía Otumba** te ofrece una narrativa profesional y validada por expertos que te otorga la libertad absoluta de caminar bajo los arcos monumentales del Padre Tembleque o explorar el ex convento a tu propio ritmo, eliminando los costos y la prisa de las excursiones masivas y los guías convencionales.

Al adquirir esta **Audioguía Otumba**, aseguras un contenido digital de máxima calidad diseñado para enriquecer el catálogo de la Megalópolis. Si buscas complementar tu ruta por el Estado de México, te sugerimos conectar esta experiencia con nuestra **[Audioguía de Tepotzotlán](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://audioguiasmexicotour.com/shop-2/tepotzotlan/)** o la **[Audioguía de Toluca](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://audioguiasmexicotour.com/shop-2/toluca/)**, optimizadas bajo los mismos estándares de rigor técnico e histórico de nuestra plataforma.

### Consejos para una Ruta por el Orgullo Histórico Mexiquense

Para disfrutar plenamente de esta **Audioguía Otumba**, te recomendamos iniciar la caminata a pie por el centro histórico durante las primeras horas de la mañana, cuando el clima es fresco y la luz resalta las tonalidades de cantera del complejo franciscano. Es fundamental usar calzado cómodo para transitar por empedrados y planificar con tiempo el traslado vehicular hacia las zonas del **Acueducto del Padre Tembleque**, donde el sol del altiplano suele ser intenso, por lo que llevar suficiente hidratación y protección solar es indispensable.

Esta **Audioguía Otumba** ha sido estructurada con un profundo respeto hacia el carácter hospitalario de una comunidad que custodia con orgullo sus leyendas virreinales, su memoria militar y sus tradiciones populares únicas. Al concluir tu jornada contemplando cómo los rayos del sol iluminan los arcos gigantescos que cruzan la meseta, entenderás por qué este destino es un tesoro indispensable para comprender la identidad cultural y el desarrollo arquitectónico de México.

Si te interesa explorar otras grandes ciudades antiguas de México, también puedes descubrir nuestras audioguías de Coba, Uxmal , Tulum y Palenque. estamos seguros que al utilizar las audioguías a la mexicana tu visita a los grandes destinos mexicanos resultará ser una fantástica inmersión histórica-cultural que hará que quieras seguir recorriendo el país A TOUR PASO porque las ciudades bonitas se disfrutan mucho mas caminándolas.

## ![](https://media.voicemap.me/assets/icons/about_new-9ee2e79b98f9d52102d4bb3aa274cc589e9ce243f2c093455ea8f54280bf6904.svg)  About the Tour

Vancouver‘s Granville Island has transformed over the past century from an industrial hub to the city‘s foremost artistic sanctuary. On this walking tour through the island (secretly a peninsula), I‘ll share its fascinating evolution.

Beginning at the iconic Granville Island Neon Sign – a nostalgic nod to Vancouver‘s 19,000 historical neon signs – and ending at the charming Go Fish seafood shack, you‘ll weave through bustling markets, quiet alleyways, and scenic boardwalks along False Creek.

Once a thriving industrial zone of factories and machinery, Granville Island now pulses with the creative energy of artisans, chefs, and performers. You‘ll discover how this unique space transitioned from First Nations fishing grounds to a manufacturing center, and finally to the cultural destination beloved by locals and visitors alike. The island retains its industrial character at places like Granville Island Public Market, which is housed in repurposed corrugated tin buildings – a perfect metaphor for Vancouver‘s ever-evolving identity.

On this leisurely 1.5-mile walk past colorful murals, waterfront views, and bustling market stalls, you‘ll also:

- Explore the vibrant Public Market where local producers showcase fresh ingredients, artisanal foods, and handcrafted goods – including the world-famous Lee‘s Donuts
- Admire the stunning _Giants_ mural, painted on six massive concrete silos by renowned Brazilian artists and twins Gustavo and Otavio Pandolfo
- Discover Railspur Alley‘s hidden artisan workshops, including a small-batch sake brewery and studios for the island‘s many sculptors and textile designers
- Learn about the former Emily Carr University of Art and Design that shaped the island‘s creative atmosphere for over 40 years
- Watch street performers in their element, from multi-instrumentalists to magicians, outside the popular bakery, A Bread Affair
- Stroll along Foreshore Walk to view False Creek Harbour‘s impressive yachts while learning about the area‘s rich marine history
- Browse the Net Loft shopping mall‘s unique stores, including the charming Paper-Ya stationery shop housed in a repurposed industrial building
- Sample fresh seafood from the Lobster Man and other fisheries that have operated on the island for decades

By the end of this walk, you’ll see how industrial heritage, artistic innovation, and culinary excellence have converged in one of Vancouver‘s most distinctive neighborhoods.

You should now be directly underneath the Granville Street bridge, and facing the inlet that runs through the city, False Creek. Stop for a minute here while I tell you a bit more about the Creek.

You should now be directly underneath the Granville Street bridge, and facing the inlet that runs through the city, False Creek. Stop for a minute here while I tell you a bit more about the Creek.

There's a funny story behind the name; Sir George Henry Richards was the hydrographer of the Royal Navy for the United Kingdom at the time, and when he was graphing the area, he assumed it was a creek. When he discovered it was actually an inlet, the "false" name stuck. There's something very Vancouver to me about Granville Island not actually being an island, and False Creek not actually being a creek: it's a city that resists easy explanation, and it definitely feels like one where an island doesn't have to really be an island to be called one.

The inlet as it looks today is mostly the result of changes made for the 1986 World Exposition held in Vancouver, better known as Expo 86. The city underwent a bunch of changes because of this world's fair, including the creation of the SkyTrain system and the Telus World of Science, and you can basically separate the city's modern history into pre-Expo and post-Expo. The shores of False Creek underwent major development, and the population in the area boomed.

If you look at your phone, I've included two photos: one of False Creek and Granville Island as they looked in 1917, and one taken just a few years after 1986. This gives you a sense of just how significant the development in the area really was.

At the time of recording in 2025, there are plenty of older generations in Vancouver that still have a lot of strong feelings about the changes made during the Expo, both good and bad; if you get the chance to chat with anyone from the city's old guard, I recommend picking their brain about it, as most younger Vancouverites, myself included, will have no memory of the city as it used to be.

While you're here, there should be a pretty solid ice cream spot opposite the Creek if you're feeling hungry at all. Otherwise, follow the boardwalk a little further with the creek on your right, and I'll catch up with you down the road.

### Places to stop along the way

While I mention several Granville Island locations by name throughout the tour, it's also well worth checking out some of the other spots that don't get a shoutout, including Siegel's Bagels and Hobbs Pickles in the market as well as Tap & Barrel on the island's northern tip for happy hour specials.

### Best time of day

This tour is best done during the peak parts of the day, 10 am-2 pm, when the shops and market are open. It's more enjoyable on a sunny day, but overcast and even rainy afternoons may mean less crowds and thus easier navigation.

### Precautions

Granville Island is a very safe part of the city, and you should have no major safety concerns. That said, sunscreen or an umbrella depending on the weather are worth considering, as well as plenty of water.

# Secret Societies of Manhattan: Magic Hunt Walking Tour & Escape Game

[4.5668 Reviews·268 people have played this quest](https://questoapp.com/new-york-city/secret-societies-of-manhattan-walking-tour-and-escape-game#abReviews)

Dive into the mysterious world of **secret societies** and **urban legends** with this immersive **walking tour and escape game** through downtown Manhattan.

As you explore iconic landmarks like the **Empire State Building**, **Rockefeller Center**, and the **NY Public Library**, you’ll also uncover hidden stories, visit **New York's oldest magic shop**, and solve puzzles that reveal some of the city’s best-kept secrets.

In this adventure, you’ll take on the role of a young reporter on the trail of a magical society hidden in Midtown. Your investigation begins at **Grand Central**, where you meet a mysterious informant who hands you everything you need for this dangerous, yet thrilling mission.

Will you discover the truth about magic in the heart of New York City? Perfect for adventurers, puzzle enthusiasts, and anyone intrigued by the city’s hidden stories, this **self-guided tour** offers a mix of history, mystery, and exploration at your own pace.

## The mission: Your story in New York City

You will play the role of a young reporter who has just moved to New York City in hopes to make their “big break.”

You’ve recently received a lead that suggests magic is here in Midtown, among some of the most popular Manhattan sights!

Your lead instructs you to meet him in Grand Central, where he’ll provide you with everything you need in order to discover a Secret Society of Magical Persons.

Yes, that sounds just like another rubbish lead (magic, pfft), except that this time your gut tells you to follow it anyway.

Be careful, magic was banished here in America over a century ago. This is a dangerous mission, but an even bigger story!

Is Secret Societies of Manhattan: Magic Hunt Walking Tour & Escape Game self-guided?

Yes. The Questo app guides you between locations without a tour guide or fixed departure. Start when it suits you and pause if needed.

Where does Secret Societies of Manhattan: Magic Hunt Walking Tour & Escape Game start and finish?

It starts at Grand central station — 89 E 42nd St, New York, NY 10017, USA and finishes at The Plaza - A Fairmont Managed Hotel — 768 5th Ave, New York, NY 10019, USA. The route is approximately 5.6 km and includes 12 location-based puzzles.

How many accesses does our group need?

This classic quest sells access per device and player. Each person who wants to solve clues on their own phone needs their own access.

What language is Secret Societies of Manhattan: Magic Hunt Walking Tour & Escape Game available in?

It is currently available to play in English.

iPhone, iPad

Turn every drive into a story.

ExploreHere is a hands-free road trip guide that plays stories automatically as you travel. Discover historic landmarks, hidden places, and unforgettable moments, without ever touching your phone.

Whether you're cruising cross-country, exploring a small town, or wandering a new city, ExploreHere reveals the stories that shaped the places around you.

Made for the Road
\- 240,000+ Historic Landmarks across the U.S.
\- Auto-Play Audio as you pass places worth knowing
\- Hands-Free Travel Mode for safe driving
\- Walking & Driving Tours through cities, parks, and scenic highways
\- Nearby History Alerts so you never miss a story

Pro Features
\- Offline access for no-service road trips
\- High-Quality Immersive Audio
\- View public lands, national parks & forests and native lands
\- Smart proximity alerts
\- Save and organize favorite stops

Perfect For
Road trippers • RV travelers • National park explorers • History lovers • Families on vacation • Curious travelers

ExploreHere transforms highways into story-filled journeys and ordinary stops into unforgettable discoveries.

See the history around you. Start exploring today.

iPhone

Geotourist is your personal tour guide for the world’s top travel attractions, landmarks and beyond.Based on your exact location access auto-play guided audio tours in multiple languages right on your smartphone. CREATE your own tours, post photos and share your experiences via social media.Your knowledge combined with augmented reality allowing you to speak to the world around you.

For Travellers: Geotourist is FREE to register and easy to use.

\- GPS Autoplay simply plays audio as you walk/travel through various locations telling you a story in
context of your location bringing your surroundings to life.

\- With GPS functionality, find the closest tours around you that are rated by other users.

\- Confidently find your way to your preferred destination from an unfamiliar location and take a tour that
guides you through audio, pictures and immersive experiences.

\- Save journeys and favourite tours in a folder to visit at later dates or for repeat visits.

\- Review, rate, and share tours with other users, friends and family through social media function.

\- Get notified of new tours published by your favourite tour guides or travel authors and travel
destinations.

\- Plan your trip ahead by searching and reviewing tours in your intended destination before travelling.

\- Take advantage of exclusive dining, shopping, accommodation and entertainment offers from
businesses around you.

\- Multiple Languages supported so you can find the right audio for you

\- Create, publish, edit and share your tour content easily through the simple web or mobile interface

\- Create your own profile account with your branding and maintain complete control over your content.

\- Publish tours for your followers and other travellers and benefit from new media channel

\- Geotourist will notify your users when you produce and publish new tour content.

\- Track how many people are following your tours.

\- Edit and enrich your tour content based on feedback from users.

\- Multiple languages supported so you can publish and reach a wide audience.

[**Ratings & Reviews**](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/948290494?see-all=reviews&platform=iphone)

out of 5







15 Ratings


- This app team fantastic. However not allowing for offline use is a giant issue. I would rate this at a five once it has that capability.

















# Could Be Perfect with Offline Use









This app team fantastic. However not allowing for offline use is a giant issue. I would rate this at a five once it has that capability.

- Downloaded to explore an annual architectural tour, and was impressed by the amount of info available on the 50 or so architecturally significant stops along the route. Also impressive were the narrated clips about each of the sites. Some of the clips needed more attention to editing (microphone clicks, mouth noises, repeated sentences), which is the only reason for 4.5 stars instead of 5. All in all, a good job!

















# Pretty good app - 4.5/5









Downloaded to explore an annual architectural tour, and was impressed by the amount of info available on the 50 or so architecturally significant stops along the route. Also impressive were the narrated clips about each of the sites. Some of the clips needed more attention to editing (microphone clicks, mouth noises, repeated sentences), which is the only reason for 4.5 stars instead of 5. All in all, a good job!

- Downloaded the app and reviewed a few tours with the hopes of creating one for a local town. It stopped working temporarily. I messaged GeoTourist and it was fixed back that afternoon. Am excited to finish the tour I’m creating and opening up local town history to visitors. Thank you!

















# No Longer Working









Downloaded the app and reviewed a few tours with the hopes of creating one for a local town. It stopped working temporarily. I messaged GeoTourist and it was fixed back that afternoon. Am excited to finish the tour I’m creating and opening up local town history to visitors. Thank you!

- Initially I had an issue creating an account on the Mobile App, but emailing customer service they checked into the issue for me, it was just a fluke. Love the Free Self-Guided Tours I’ve tried so far.

















# Responsive customer service, great tour of the Gaslamp Quarter in San Diego, Ca









Initially I had an issue creating an account on the Mobile App, but emailing customer service they checked into the issue for me, it was just a fluke. Love the Free Self-Guided Tours I’ve tried so far.

- This app would do everything I need it to if it worked. Seems like there is no support anymore? No locations can ever be found, so I added all points manually. Once all done, I can't save as it says a bunch of info is missing although all fields are filled out. Can someone please help? Thanks!

















# Ugh









This app would do everything I need it to if it worked. Seems like there is no support anymore? No locations can ever be found, so I added all points manually. Once all done, I can't save as it says a bunch of info is missing although all fields are filled out. Can someone please help? Thanks!

- Just downloaded today and went through narrated Atlanta tour. Superb. I couldn’t find a way to rate the individual tours however.

















# Excellent Narrated Tours









Just downloaded today and went through narrated Atlanta tour. Superb. I couldn’t find a way to rate the individual tours however.

- I had full signal, all permissions on, but I was only able to hear three of the 22 clips on my tour. What I heard was good but it was quite frustrating to hear so little and stand around waiting for clips that never loaded.

















# Clips just didn’t load









I had full signal, all permissions on, but I was only able to hear three of the 22 clips on my tour. What I heard was good but it was quite frustrating to hear so little and stand around waiting for clips that never loaded.

- I took longer downloading this than using it. Search icon brought up a blank screen and no keyboard…

I took longer downloading this than using it. Search icon brought up a blank screen and no keyboard…
